title: PoisonedRAG: Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Zou, Wei and Geng, Runpeng and Wang, Binghui and Jia, Jinyuan
actual_contribution: Introduces PoisonedRAG, the first knowledge-corruption attack on RAG, formulating malicious-text crafting as an optimization with retrieval and generation conditions, achieving high ASRs in black-box and white-box settings across datasets and LLMs.

title: Certifiably Robust RAG against Retrieval Corruption
authors: Chong Xiang and Tong Wu and Zexuan Zhong and David Wagner and Danqi Chen and Prateek Mittal
actual_contribution: RobustRAG introduces an isolate-then-aggregate defense (keyword and decoding aggregation) providing certifiable robustness guarantees against bounded retrieval corruption attacks in RAG.

title: Making Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Robust to Irrelevant Context
authors: Ori Yoran and Tomer Wolfson and Ori Ram and Jonathan Berant
actual_contribution: Shows RALMs are brittle to irrelevant retrieved context and proposes two mitigations: NLI-based filtering of non-entailing passages and fine-tuning on mixed relevant/irrelevant contexts to teach robust use of retrieval in single- and multi-hop QA.

title: Enhancing Noise Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Adaptive Adversarial Training
authors: Fang, Feiteng and Bai, Yuelin and Ni, Shiwen and Yang, Min and Chen, Xiaojun and Xu, Ruifeng
actual_contribution: Categorizes retrieval noise into relevant, irrelevant, and counterfactual types, proposes RAAT (adaptive adversarial training with noise-aware multi-task learning), and introduces RAG-Bench for evaluating noise robustness on three open-domain QA datasets.

title: Phantom: General Backdoor Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Language Generation
authors: Harsh Chaudhari and Giorgio Severi and John Abascal and Anshuman Suri and Matthew Jagielski and Christopher A. Choquette-Choo and Milad Nasr and Cristina Nita-Rotaru and Alina Oprea
actual_contribution: Phantom is a backdoor poisoning attack on RAG that uses a two-stage optimization (HotFlip on retriever + Multi-Coordinate Gradient on generator) to craft a single poisoned document retrieved only when a natural trigger appears in the query, enabling refusal, biased opinion, harmful behavior, passage exfiltration, and tool misuse across open and closed LLMs including a black-box attack on NVIDIA ChatRTX.

title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Vinh Nguyen and Cuong Dang and Jiahao Zhang and Hoa Tran and Minh Tran and Trinh Chau and Thai Le and Lu Cheng and Suhang Wang
benchmark_or_task: Evaluation and Benchmarks / Calibration and Uncertainty
actual_contribution: Introduces URAG, a benchmark that reformulates open-ended RAG tasks into MCQA and applies conformal prediction to jointly evaluate accuracy and uncertainty of 8 RAG methods across 5 domains, including under irrelevant/noisy retrieval.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Primary focus is uncertainty quantification benchmark; noisy retrieval is one experimental dimension

title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
authors: Xi Zhu and Ziqi Wang and Kai Mei and Wujiang Xu and Minghao Guo and Bangji Yang and Jiajun Fan and Dimitris N. Metaxas
actual_contribution: Proposes SABER, a frozen-LLM probe combining self-prior and source-conditional reasoning representations to estimate PK/CK reliability and drive a 4-cell trust/abstain decision; also builds a ground-truth-aligned knowledge-conflict benchmark with faithfulness metrics.

title: The First Drop of Ink: Nonlinear Impact of Misleading Information in Long-Context Reasoning
authors: Muhan Gao and Zih-Ching Chen and Kuan-Hao Huang
actual_contribution: Identifies a nonlinear 'first drop of ink' effect where a small fraction of hard distractors in long contexts disproportionately degrades QA accuracy, with theoretical analysis via attention/softmax mechanics and validation on retrieval heads.

title: ProGRank: Probe-Gradient Reranking to Defend Dense-Retriever RAG from Corpus Poisoning
authors: Xiangyu Yin and Yi Qi and Chih-Hong Cheng
actual_contribution: Proposes ProGRank, a training-free retriever-side reranking defense that uses probe-gradient instability signals under randomized perturbations to demote poisoned passages in dense-retriever RAG.

title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
authors: Hongyan Chang and Ergute Bao and Xinjian Luo and Ting Yu
actual_contribution: Proposes a black-box CEM-based prefix optimization to guarantee retrieval of injected malicious documents (trigger fragment + attack fragment), enabling end-to-end indirect prompt injection attacks against RAG and agentic systems, evaluated across 11 BEIR benchmarks and 8 embedding models.

title: Over-Searching in Search-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Roy Xie and Deepak Gopinath and David Qiu and Dong Lin and Haitian Sun and Saloni Potdar and Bhuwan Dhingra
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve and Abstain
actual_contribution: Defines and systematically evaluates over-searching in search-augmented LLMs, introduces the Tokens Per Correctness (TPC) metric, and releases the OverSearchQA benchmark for abstention/efficiency evaluation.

title: NAACL: Noise-AwAre Verbal Confidence Calibration for Robust LLMs in RAG Systems
authors: Jiayu Liu and Rui Wang and Qing Zong and Yumeng Wang and Cheng Qian and Qingcheng Zeng and Tianshi Zheng and Haochen Shi and Dadi Guo and Baixuan Xu and Chunyang Li and Yangqiu Song
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control under Noisy Retrieval
actual_contribution: Proposes NAACL, an SFT framework with noise-aware rules (conflict independence, noise invariance, parametric fallback) that calibrates verbal confidence of LLMs in RAG under irrelevant/counterfactual retrieval, improving ECE substantially.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Primary contribution is calibration; noisy retrieval is the diagnostic lens, so inclusion is justified but secondary.

title: CoRect: Context-Aware Logit Contrast for Hidden State Rectification to Resolve Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Xuhua Ma and Richong Zhang and Zhijie Nie
actual_contribution: CoRect is a training-free, target-agnostic method that uses context-aware logit contrast to localize FFN layers exhibiting 'parametric suppression' and rectifies their hidden states to resolve knowledge conflicts in RAG, improving QA and summarization faithfulness.

title: CleanBase: Detecting Malicious Documents in RAG Knowledge Databases
authors: Weifei Jin and Xilong Wang and Wei Zou and Jinyuan Jia and Neil Gong
actual_contribution: Proposes CleanBase, a defense that detects malicious documents in a RAG knowledge database by constructing a similarity graph and identifying cliques of semantically similar injected documents, with theoretical FPR/FNR bounds.

title: AdversarialCoT: Single-Document Retrieval Poisoning for LLM Reasoning
authors: Hongru Song and Yu-An Liu and Ruqing Zhang and Jiafeng Guo and Maarten de Rijke and Yixing Fan and Xueqi Cheng
actual_contribution: Introduces AdversarialCoT, a query-specific single-document poisoning attack that iteratively crafts adversarial chain-of-thought documents to mislead retrieval-augmented LLM reasoning under a black-box setting.

title: Addressing Corpus Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG Using Sparse Attention
authors: Sagie Dekel and Moshe Tennenholtz and Oren Kurland
actual_contribution: Proposes Sparse Document Attention RAG (SDAG), a block-sparse attention defense at inference time that disables cross-document attention to mitigate corpus poisoning attacks, outperforming SOTA defenses.

title: AIP: Subverting Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Adversarial Instructional Prompt
authors: Chaturvedi, Saket S. and Bagwe, Gaurav and Zhang, Lan and Yuan, Xiaoyong
actual_contribution: Introduces AIP, a black-box attack that crafts natural-looking adversarial instructional prompts (paired with poisoned documents and a stealthy trigger) to covertly steer RAG retrieval and generation toward attacker-targeted outputs while preserving clean-task utility.

title: Why Uncertainty Estimation Methods Fall Short in RAG: An Axiomatic Analysis
authors: Heydar Soudani and Evangelos Kanoulas and Faegheh Hasibi
actual_contribution: Analyzes failure modes of uncertainty estimation methods in RAG setups, defines five axioms an effective UE method should satisfy with retrieved context, and derives a calibration function that improves AUROC.

title: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Huichi Zhou and Kin-Hei Lee and Zhonghao Zhan and Yue Chen and Zhenhao Li and Zhaoyang Wang and Hamed Haddadi and Emine Yilmaz
actual_contribution: TrustRAG is a two-stage defense framework against RAG corpus poisoning that uses K-means clustering with ROUGE-based filtering to remove tightly-clustered malicious documents, then resolves conflicts between internal LLM knowledge and external retrieved evidence via self-assessment.
limitation_or_note: Knowledge conflict and contextual faithfulness: Primarily an adversarial-corruption defense, but it explicitly addresses knowledge conflict resolution as a core mechanism.

title: Traceback of Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang and Haoran Xin and Minghong Fang and Zhuqing Liu and Biao Yi and Tong Li and Zheli Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes RAGForensics, a traceback system that iteratively retrieves and LLM-classifies poisoned texts in RAG knowledge bases responsible for incorrect outputs, evaluated against PoisonedRAG and instruction injection attacks plus adaptive variants.

title: Through the Stealth Lens: Attention-Aware Defenses Against Poisoning in RAG
authors: Sarthak Choudhary and Nils Palumbo and Ashish Hooda and Krishnamurthy Dj Dvijotham and Somesh Jha
actual_contribution: Formalizes a stealth distinguishability game for RAG poisoning and proposes an attention-variance filter (AV Filter) using NPAS to detect and remove poisoned passages, plus adaptive attacks to evade it.

title: Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation against Poisoning Attacks
authors: Zirui Cheng and Jikai Sun and Anjun Gao and Yueyang Quan and Zhuqing Liu and Xiaohua Hu and Minghong Fang
actual_contribution: Proposes RAGuard, a defense against RAG knowledge-base poisoning that combines retrieval expansion with chunk-wise perplexity and text similarity filtering to detect and remove poisoned texts.

title: SeCon-RAG: A Two-Stage Semantic Filtering and Conflict-Free Framework for Trustworthy RAG
authors: Xiaonan Si and Meilin Zhu and Simeng Qin and Lijia Yu and Lijun Zhang and Shuaitong Liu and Xinfeng Li and Ranjie Duan and Yang Liu and Xiaojun Jia
actual_contribution: SeCon-RAG defends against corpus poisoning via a two-stage pipeline combining clustering+semantic-graph filtering (via an Entity-Intent-Relation Extractor) and a conflict-aware filtering module that resolves contradictions between query, retrieved documents, and the LLM's internal knowledge.

title: Safeguarding RAG Pipelines with GMTP: A Gradient-based Masked Token Probability Method for Poisoned Document Detection
authors: San Kim and Jonghwi Kim and Yejin Jeon and Gary Geunbae Lee
actual_contribution: GMTP defends RAG against corpus poisoning by identifying high-gradient tokens, masking them, and using an MLM to detect anomalously low predicted probabilities indicative of injected adversarial tokens.

title: SafeRAG: Benchmarking Security in Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Model
authors: Xun Liang and Simin Niu and Zhiyu Li and Sensen Zhang and Hanyu Wang and Feiyu Xiong and Jason Zhaoxin Fan and Bo Tang and Shichao Song and Mengwei Wang and Jiawei Yang
actual_contribution: SafeRAG is a Chinese benchmark for evaluating RAG security against four adversarial attack tasks (silver noise, inter-context conflict, soft ad, white DoS) injected at various pipeline stages.

title: Rescuing the Unpoisoned: Efficient Defense against Knowledge Corruption Attacks on RAG Systems
authors: Minseok Kim and Hankook Lee and Hyungjoon Koo
actual_contribution: Proposes RAGDefender, a lightweight post-retrieval defense that clusters and filters adversarial passages to mitigate knowledge corruption (poisoning) attacks on RAG systems.

title: ReliabilityRAG: Effective and Provably Robust Defense for RAG-based Web-Search
authors: Zeyu Shen and Basileal Imana and Tong Wu and Chong Xiang and Prateek Mittal and Aleksandra Korolova
actual_contribution: Proposes ReliabilityRAG, a defense against retrieval corruption (corpus poisoning, prompt injection) using a Maximum Independent Set over a contradiction graph that leverages document reliability/rank, with provable robustness guarantees and a scalable weighted sample-and-aggregate variant.

title: RAGPart \& RAGMask: Retrieval-Stage Defenses Against Corpus Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Pankayaraj Pathmanathan and Michael-Andrei Panaitescu-Liess and Cho-Yu Jason Chiang and Furong Huang
actual_contribution: Introduces two retrieval-stage defenses (RAGPart via fragment partitioning/averaging and RAGMask via token-masking similarity shifts) against corpus poisoning in RAG, plus an interpretable AdvRAGgen attack.

title: PoisonArena: Uncovering Competing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Liuji Chen and Xiaofang Yang and Yuanzhuo Lu and Jinghao Zhang and Xin Sun and Qiang Liu and Shu Wu and Jing Dong and Liang Wang
actual_contribution: Introduces PoisonArena, a benchmark for evaluating competing poisoning attacks in RAG using a Bradley-Terry model, showing that strong single-attacker methods often fail under multi-attacker competition.

title: ParamMute: Suppressing Knowledge-Critical FFNs for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Pengcheng Huang and Zhenghao Liu and Yukun Yan and Haiyan Zhao and Xiaoyuan Yi and Hao Chen and Zhiyuan Liu and Maosong Sun and Tong Xiao and Ge Yu and Chenyan Xiong
actual_contribution: Identifies a subset of mid-to-deep FFN layers that drive unfaithful generation in RAG, proposes suppression + preference optimization (ParamMute) to enhance contextual faithfulness, and introduces the CoFaithfulQA benchmark for evaluating faithfulness under knowledge conflicts.

title: PR-Attack: Coordinated Prompt-RAG Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models via Bilevel Optimization
authors: Yang Jiao and Xiaodong Wang and Kai Yang
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks
actual_contribution: Introduces PR-Attack, a bilevel-optimization-based coordinated poisoning attack on RAG-based LLMs that jointly optimizes a small number of poisoned documents and a backdoor trigger in the prompt to achieve stealthy, high-ASR attacks.

title: POISONCRAFT: Practical Poisoning of Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models
authors: Yangguang Shao and Xinjie Lin and Haozheng Luo and Chengshang Hou and Gang Xiong and Jiahao Yu and Junzheng Shi
actual_contribution: Proposes POISONCRAFT, a query-agnostic poisoning attack on RAG that injects optimized adversarial documents to make LLMs recommend a malicious URL, demonstrating effectiveness, transferability across retrievers, and robustness against defenses.

title: Magic Mushroom: A Customizable Benchmark for Fine-grained Analysis of Retrieval Noise Erosion in RAG Systems
authors: Yuxin Zhang and Yan Wang and Yongrui Chen and Shenyu Zhang and Xinbang Dai and Sheng Bi and Guilin Qi
actual_contribution: Introduces Magic Mushroom, a customizable QA benchmark with four fine-grained retrieval noise types (distracting, low-quality, inconsequential, irrelevant) for evaluating RAG robustness under configurable noise distributions.

title: MIRAGE: Misleading Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Black-box and Query-agnostic Poisoning Attacks
authors: Tailun Chen and Yu He and Yan Wang and Shuo Shao and Haolun Zheng and Zhihao Liu and Jinfeng Li and Zhizhen Qin and Yuefeng Chen and Zhixuan Chu and Zhan Qin and Kui Ren
actual_contribution: Proposes MIRAGE, a black-box, query-agnostic RAG corpus poisoning attack using persona-driven query synthesis, semantic anchoring, and adversarial test-time preference optimization, evaluated on a new long-form domain-specific benchmark.
limitation_or_note: Adversarial corruption and security.: Assigned categories include evaluation_benchmark, which is also supported as the paper builds a dedicated long-form RAG poisoning benchmark, but the manuscript only cites it under adversarial corruption.

title: MAGIC: A Multi-Hop and Graph-Based Benchmark for Inter-Context Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jungyeon Lee and Kangmin Lee and Taeuk Kim
actual_contribution: Introduces MAGIC, a knowledge-graph-based benchmark for evaluating inter-context knowledge conflict detection in RAG, featuring multi-hop and multi-conflict scenarios.

title: FaithfulRAG: Fact-Level Conflict Modeling for Context-Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhang, Qinggang and Xiang, Zhishang and Xiao, Yilin and Wang, Le and Li, Junhui and Wang, Xinrun and Su, Jinsong
actual_contribution: FaithfulRAG resolves parametric vs. retrieved knowledge conflicts by mining self-facts, aligning them with retrieved context chunks, and running a self-think module to reconcile discrepancies before generation.

title: Do Retrieval Augmented Language Models Know When They Don't Know?
authors: Youchao Zhou and Heyan Huang and Yicheng Liu and Rui Dai and Xinglin Wang and Xingchen Zhang and Shumin Shi and Yang Deng
actual_contribution: Investigates whether retrieval-augmented LLMs are well-calibrated and know when to refuse, finding that purely irrelevant retrieved contexts induce over-refusal and miscalibration; proposes uncertainty-based two-stage refusal mechanism.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper also strongly fits calibration_control and ood_uncertainty (assigned), and addresses noisy retrieval specifically through impact of irrelevant documents.

title: DRAGged into Conflicts: Detecting and Addressing Conflicting Sources in Search-Augmented LLMs
authors: Arie Cattan and Alon Jacovi and Ori Ram and Jonathan Herzig and Roee Aharoni and Sasha Goldshtein and Eran Ofek and Idan Szpektor and Avi Caciularu
actual_contribution: Introduces a taxonomy of inter-context knowledge conflict types in RAG (no conflict, complementary, conflicting opinions, outdated, misinformation) and the CONFLICTS benchmark with expert annotations, showing LLMs struggle to adopt type-appropriate responses.

title: CUB: Benchmarking Context Utilisation Techniques for Language Models
authors: Lovisa Hagström and Youna Kim and Haeun Yu and Sang-goo Lee and Richard Johansson and Hyunsoo Cho and Isabelle Augenstein
actual_contribution: CUB benchmarks seven context-utilisation manipulation techniques across 11 LMs on CounterFact, NQ, and DRUID under gold, conflicting, and irrelevant contexts, revealing trade-offs between faithfulness and robustness.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Paper covers knowledge conflict and distraction/irrelevant context evaluation; fits all assigned categories.

title: Benchmarking Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang and Haoran Xin and Jiatong Li and Dongzhe Zhang and Minghong Fang and Zhuqing Liu and Lihai Nie and Zheli Liu
actual_contribution: Introduces RSB, a benchmark covering 13 poisoning attacks and 7 defenses against RAG across 15 QA datasets and multiple RAG architectures, with comprehensive empirical analysis.

title: Adaptive Retrieval Without Self-Knowledge? Bringing Uncertainty Back Home
authors: Viktor Moskvoretskii and Maria Lysyuk and Mikhail Salnikov and Nikolay Ivanov and Sergey Pletenev and Daria Galimzianova and Nikita Krayko and Vasily Konovalov and Irina Nikishina and Alexander Panchenko
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Benchmarks 35 adaptive retrieval methods (8 recent pipelines + 27 uncertainty estimation methods) across 6 QA datasets with 10 metrics covering QA accuracy, efficiency (LLM/retrieval calls), and self-knowledge, showing UE methods match complex adaptive RAG pipelines at lower cost.

title: Glue pizza and eat rocks - Exploiting Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generative Models
authors: Zhen Tan and Chengshuai Zhao and Raha Moraffah and Yifan Li and Song Wang and Jundong Li and Tianlong Chen and Huan Liu
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial corruption: poisoning and injection attacks
actual_contribution: Introduces LIAR, a bi-level optimization attack that crafts adversarial documents which are both preferentially retrieved and cause LLMs to produce harmful or enforced outputs, demonstrating RAG vulnerability in a gray-box setting.

title: WikiContradict: A Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs on Real-World Knowledge Conflicts from Wikipedia
authors: Yufang Hou and Alessandra Pascale and Javier Carnerero-Cano and Tigran Tchrakian and Radu Marinescu and Elizabeth Daly and Inkit Padhi and Prasanna Sattigeri
actual_contribution: Presents WikiContradict, a Wikipedia-based benchmark of 253 annotated instances with contradictory passages, used to evaluate how LLMs handle real-world inter-context knowledge conflicts in RAG settings.

title: Toward Robust RALMs: Revealing the Impact of Imperfect Retrieval on Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Seong-Il Park and Jay-Yoon Lee
taxonomy_categories: noisy_retrieval; distraction; knowledge_conflict; adversarial_corruption; ood_uncertainty; evaluation_benchmark
failure_or_risk_type: retrieval noise/distraction; knowledge conflict/faithfulness; adversarial corruption; uncertainty/unanswerability
benchmark_or_task: Evaluation and benchmarks for robust RAG
actual_contribution: Systematically evaluates RALM robustness against unanswerable, adversarial, and conflicting retrieved documents, introducing GenADV adversarial passage generation and the RAD robustness metric for open-domain QA.

title: To Trust or Not to Trust? Enhancing Large Language Models' Situated Faithfulness to External Contexts
authors: Yukun Huang and Sanxing Chen and Hongyi Cai and Bhuwan Dhingra
actual_contribution: Introduces 'situated faithfulness' and benchmarks LLMs on QA with correct/incorrect contexts (including new RedditQA), proposing Self-Guided and Rule-Based Confidence Reasoning plus CR-DPO to calibrate trust between internal knowledge and external context.

title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Hailey Joren and Jianyi Zhang and Chun-Sung Ferng and Da-Cheng Juan and Ankur Taly and Cyrus Rashtchian
actual_contribution: Introduces 'sufficient context' as a property of (query, context) pairs, builds an LLM autorater to label it, analyzes RAG hallucination/abstention behavior stratified by sufficiency, and proposes a selective generation method combining sufficiency with self-confidence to reduce hallucinations.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Primary contribution is answerability/calibration/abstention rather than distraction or compression per se.

title: Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG: Overcoming Challenges for Long Inputs in RAG
authors: Bowen Jin and Jinsung Yoon and Jiawei Han and Sercan O. Arik
actual_contribution: Empirically shows long-context RAG performance follows an inverted-U as retrieved passages increase due to hard negatives, and proposes retrieval reordering plus RAG-specific fine-tuning (implicit and reasoning-augmented) to improve robustness.

title: FaithEval: Can Your Language Model Stay Faithful to Context, Even If "The Moon is Made of Marshmallows"
authors: Yifei Ming and Senthil Purushwalkam and Shrey Pandit and Zixuan Ke and Xuan-Phi Nguyen and Caiming Xiong and Shafiq Joty
actual_contribution: Introduces FaithEval, a 4.9K-sample benchmark evaluating LLM contextual faithfulness under unanswerable, inconsistent, and counterfactual contexts, showing even SOTA models struggle to remain faithful to provided contexts.

title: Controlling Risk of Retrieval-augmented Generation: A Counterfactual Prompting Framework
authors: Lu Chen and Ruqing Zhang and Jiafeng Guo and Yixing Fan and Xueqi Cheng
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and control: abstention in RAG
actual_contribution: Proposes a counterfactual prompting framework to assess RAG predictive uncertainty by perturbing retrieval quality and usage, with a new benchmark and risk-aware metrics for abstention.

title: Context-DPO: Aligning Language Models for Context-Faithfulness
authors: Baolong Bi and Shaohan Huang and Yiwei Wang and Tianchi Yang and Zihan Zhang and Haizhen Huang and Lingrui Mei and Junfeng Fang and Zehao Li and Furu Wei and Weiwei Deng and Feng Sun and Qi Zhang and Shenghua Liu
actual_contribution: Introduces ConFiQA, a benchmark for evaluating context-faithfulness under knowledge conflicts in RAG, and Context-DPO, a DPO-based alignment method that improves LLMs' adherence to provided counterfactual context.

title: Why So Gullible? Enhancing the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Models against Counterfactual Noise
authors: Giwon Hong and Jeonghwan Kim and Junmo Kang and Sung-Hyon Myaeng and Joyce Jiyoung Whang
actual_contribution: Shows that retrieval-augmented LMs (FiD, GPT-3.5) are brittle to counterfactual/conflicting documents, proposes a discriminator-based fine-tuning and prompting approach to improve robustness, and releases MACNOISE, an LLM-generated knowledge-conflict benchmark.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper is primarily about knowledge conflict / counterfactual noise rather than generic noisy retrieval or context compression, but conflict-induced noise reasonably fits the noisy retrieval category.

title: Learning to Filter Context for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhiruo Wang and Jun Araki and Zhengbao Jiang and Md Rizwan Parvez and Graham Neubig
actual_contribution: FILCO proposes sentence-level context filtering for RAG using STRINC, lexical overlap, and CXMI measures to remove distracting content from retrieved passages, training a filter model and showing gains across six knowledge-intensive tasks.

title: Investigating the Factual Knowledge Boundary of Large Language Models with Retrieval Augmentation
authors: Ruiyang Ren and Yuhao Wang and Yingqi Qu and Wayne Xin Zhao and Jing Liu and Hao Tian and Hua Wu and Ji-Rong Wen and Haifeng Wang
actual_contribution: Empirical study of LLMs' perception of factual knowledge boundaries via priori/posteriori judgement, showing overconfidence, poor handling of internal-external knowledge conflicts, and improvements from retrieval augmentation, including a dynamic retrieval strategy based on self-judgement.

title: Chain-of-Note: Enhancing Robustness in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Wenhao Yu and Hongming Zhang and Xiaoman Pan and Kaixin Ma and Hongwei Wang and Dong Yu
actual_contribution: Introduces Chain-of-Note, which has RALMs generate per-document reading notes to assess relevance, leverage intrinsic knowledge, and abstain ('unknown') when evidence is insufficient, improving noise and unknown robustness across open-domain QA benchmarks.

title: Benchmarking Large Language Models in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Chen, Jiawei and Lin, Hongyu and Han, Xianpei and Sun, Le
actual_contribution: Introduces RGB, a bilingual benchmark evaluating LLM RAG along four abilities: noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness.

title: Adaptive Chameleon or Stubborn Sloth: Revealing the Behavior of Large Language Models in Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Jian Xie and Kai Zhang and Jiangjie Chen and Renze Lou and Yu Su
actual_contribution: Proposes a framework to elicit parametric memory and construct coherent counter-memory, then analyzes LLM behavior in knowledge conflicts, finding high receptiveness to coherent counter-evidence but confirmation bias when memory-aligned evidence coexists.

title: CPA-RAG: Covert Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Large Language Models
authors: Chunyang Li and Junwei Zhang and Anda Cheng and Zhuo Ma and Xinghua Li and Jianfeng Ma
actual_contribution: Introduces CPA-RAG, a black-box covert poisoning attack on RAG that uses multi-LLM prompt-based generation and retriever-aware optimization to craft fluent adversarial passages that evade common defenses.

title: Poisoning Retrieval Corpora by Injecting Adversarial Passages
authors: Zhong, Zexuan and Huang, Ziqing and Wettig, Alexander and Chen, Danqi
actual_contribution: Introduces a HotFlip-based corpus poisoning attack that crafts a small number of adversarial passages to be retrieved by dense retrievers for broad and out-of-domain query distributions, exposing vulnerabilities in Contriever, DPR, ANCE, and ColBERT.

title: ] Typos that Broke the RAG's Back: Genetic Attack on RAG Pipeline by Simulating Documents in the Wild via Low-level Perturbations
authors: Sukmin Cho and Soyeong Jeong and Jeongyeon Seo and Taeho Hwang and Jong C. Park
actual_contribution: Proposes GARAG, a black-box genetic algorithm that injects low-level typo perturbations into retrieved documents to jointly attack retriever and reader in RAG, showing significant performance degradation across QA datasets.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper is primarily an adversarial corruption attack; it also relates to noisy retrieval since perturbations simulate naturally noisy documents.

title: UniC-RAG: Universal Knowledge Corruption Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Runpeng Geng and Yanting Wang and Ying Chen and Jinyuan Jia
actual_contribution: Proposes UniC-RAG, a universal knowledge corruption attack that jointly optimizes a small set of adversarial passages (via balanced similarity-based clustering and HotFlip) to compromise many diverse user queries in a RAG knowledge base, evaluating across datasets, retrievers, LLMs, and defenses.

title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
authors: Zhou, Yujia and Zhang, Wenbo and Shao, Jingying and Liu, Yan and Li, Xiaoxi and Jin, Jiajie and Qian, Hongjin and Liu, Zheng and Li, Chaozhuo and Zhang, Jason Chen and Dou, Zhicheng and Yu, Philip S. and Mao, Jiaxin
actual_contribution: Survey of trustworthiness in RAG across six dimensions (factuality, robustness, fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy) with a benchmark (TRC Bench) evaluating 19 LLMs.

title: TrojanRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Can Be Backdoor Driver in Large Language Models
authors: Cheng, Pengzhou and Ding, Yidong and Ju, Tianjie and Wu, Zongru and Du, Wei and Yi, Ping and Zhang, Zhuosheng and Liu, Gongshen
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Backdoors and Poisoning in RAG
actual_contribution: Proposes TrojanRAG, a backdoor attack on the RAG retriever using contrastive learning and knowledge-graph-enhanced poisoned contexts to make triggered queries induce targeted, biased, or jailbreaking LLM outputs while keeping LLM weights untouched.

title: Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
authors: Ni, Bo and Liu, Zheyuan and Wang, Leyao and Lei, Yongjia and Zhao, Yuying and Cheng, Xueqi and Zeng, Qingkai and Dong, Luna and Xia, Yinglong and Kenthapadi, Krishnaram and Rossi, Ryan and Dernoncourt, Franck and Tanjim, Md Mehrab and Ahmed, Nesreen and Liu, Xiaorui and Fan, Wenqi and Blasch, Erik and Wang, Yu and Jiang, Meng and Derr, Tyler
actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of trustworthy RAG systems organized around six pillars (reliability, privacy, safety, fairness, explainability, accountability), with taxonomies, evaluation protocols, and applications in healthcare, law, and education.
limitation_or_note: Adversarial corruption and security.: This is a survey, not a primary adversarial-corruption work; it covers safety as one of many axes.

title: Joint-GCG: Unified Gradient-Based Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Haowei Wang and Rupeng Zhang and Junjie Wang and Mingyang Li and Yuekai Huang and Dandan Wang and Qing Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes Joint-GCG, a unified gradient-based corpus poisoning attack on RAG that jointly optimizes retriever and generator objectives via cross-vocabulary projection, gradient tokenization alignment, and adaptive weighted fusion.

title: GraphRAG under Fire
authors: Liang, Jiacheng and Wang, Yuhui and Li, Changjiang and Jiang, Tanqiu and Zhu, Rongyi and Gong, Neil and Wang, Ting
actual_contribution: Introduces GRAGPOISON, a black-box poisoning attack tailored to GraphRAG that injects/enhances false relations to compromise multiple multi-hop queries simultaneously, and evaluates defenses.

title: Eyes-on-Me: Scalable RAG Poisoning through Transferable Attention-Steering Attractors
authors: Yen-Shan Chen and Sian-Yao Huang and Cheng-Lin Yang and Yun-Nung Chen
actual_contribution: Proposes EYES-ON-ME, a modular RAG poisoning attack using reusable attention attractors that steer influential attention heads toward a focus region containing swappable payloads, achieving high attack success and transferability across retrievers/generators.

title: BadRAG: Identifying Vulnerabilities in Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Jiaqi Xue and Mengxin Zheng and Yebowen Hu and Fei Liu and Xun Chen and Qian Lou
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial corruption: poisoning and retrieval backdoors
actual_contribution: BadRAG crafts adversarial passages via contrastive optimization that are retrieved only for trigger queries, enabling DoS and sentiment-steering attacks on RAG-based LLMs with minimal poisoning ratio.

title: AgentPoison: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
authors: Zhaorun Chen and Zhen Xiang and Chaowei Xiao and Dawn Song and Bo Li
actual_contribution: Proposes AgentPoison, a backdoor attack on RAG-based LLM agents that optimizes triggers via constrained optimization to map triggered queries into a unique embedding region, ensuring high retrieval of malicious demonstrations and adversarial action generation.

title: ADMIT: Few-shot Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based Fact Checking
authors: Yutao Wu and Xiao Liu and Yinghui Li and Yifeng Gao and Yifan Ding and Jiale Ding and Xiang Zheng and Xingjun Ma
actual_contribution: Introduces ADMIT, a few-shot adversarial passage injection attack on RAG-based fact-checking systems that flips verification decisions across retrievers, LLMs, and domains under black-box access.

title: Worse than Zero-shot? A Fact-Checking Dataset for Evaluating the Robustness of RAG Against Misleading Retrievals
authors: Linda Zeng and Rithwik Gupta and Divij Motwani and Yi Zhang and Diji Yang
benchmark_or_task: Benchmarks for misleading retrieval and knowledge conflict
actual_contribution: Introduces RAGUARD, a political fact-checking benchmark with Reddit-sourced documents labeled as supporting, misleading, or unrelated, showing that LLM RAG systems perform worse than zero-shot baselines under misleading retrievals.

title: Tug-of-War Between Knowledge: Exploring and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Zhuoran Jin and Pengfei Cao and Yubo Chen and Kang Liu and Xiaojian Jiang and Jiexin Xu and Qiuxia Li and Jun Zhao
actual_contribution: Proposes an evaluation framework for knowledge conflicts in RALMs (internal vs. external and among external evidence), reveals Dunning-Kruger-like and confirmation bias behaviors, and introduces Conflict-Disentangle Contrastive Decoding (CD2) to calibrate model confidence.

title: TrustRAG: Enhancing Robustness and Trustworthiness in RAG
authors: Zhou, Huichi and Lee, Kin-Hei and Zhan, Zhonghao and Li, Zhenhao and Chen, Yue and Wang, Zhaoyang and Haddadi, Hamed and Yilmaz, Emine
actual_contribution: TrustRAG is a two-stage defense framework (K-means clustering + ROUGE filtering, then internal-knowledge conflict resolution) that mitigates single- and multi-document corpus poisoning attacks in RAG systems.

title: RAGTruth: A Hallucination Corpus for Developing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Niu, Cheng and Wu, Yuanhao and Zhu, Juno and Xu, Siliang and Shum, Kashun and Zhong, Randy and Song, Juntong and Zhang, Tong
actual_contribution: RAGTruth is a ~18K-response corpus with word-level hallucination annotations across QA, data-to-text, and summarization in RAG settings, used to benchmark hallucination detection methods and fine-tune detectors.

title: Practical Poisoning Attacks against Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang and Yuxi Chen and Zhuqing Liu and Lihai Nie and Tong Li and Zheli Liu and Minghong Fang
actual_contribution: CorruptRAG is a practical single-text poisoning attack on RAG that uses adversarial templates (CorruptRAG-AS) and LLM-refined adversarial knowledge (CorruptRAG-AK) to manipulate generated answers, outperforming prior multi-text poisoning baselines and resisting four defenses.

title: Astute RAG: Overcoming Imperfect Retrieval Augmentation and Knowledge Conflicts for Large Language Models
authors: Wang, Fei and Wan, Xingchen and Sun, Ruoxi and Chen, Jiefeng and Arik, Sercan O.
actual_contribution: Proposes ASTUTE RAG, a training-free method that elicits LLM internal knowledge, performs iterative source-aware consolidation with retrieved passages to resolve conflicts, and selects the final answer by reliability comparison; demonstrates worst-case robustness under imperfect retrieval.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression: Paper's primary focus is knowledge conflict resolution; it fits noisy retrieval too but is more centrally a knowledge_conflict/calibration paper.

title: Redefining Retrieval Evaluation in the Era of LLMs
authors: Giovanni Trappolini and Florin Cuconasu and Simone Filice and Yoelle Maarek and Fabrizio Silvestri
benchmark_or_task: Evaluation and Metrics for Robust RAG
actual_contribution: Introduces UDCG, a utility- and distraction-aware retrieval evaluation metric that aligns IR scoring with LLM-consumer behavior, showing stronger correlation with end-to-end RAG accuracy than nDCG/MAP/MRR.

title: Epistemic Bias Injection: Biasing LLMs via Selective Context Retrieval
authors: Hao Wu and Prateek Saxena
actual_contribution: Proposes EBI, a stealthy RAG corpus poisoning attack that injects factually correct yet epistemically biased passages, introduces a polarization-score metric, builds an evaluation benchmark, and proposes BiasDef defense.

title: When Safety Becomes a Vulnerability: Exploiting LLM Alignment Homogeneity for Transferable Blocking in RAG
authors: Junchen Li and Chao Qi and Rongzheng Wang and Qizhi Chen and Liang Xu and Di Liang and Bob Simons and Shuang Liang
actual_contribution: Introduces TabooRAG, a black-box transferable blocking (denial-of-service) attack on RAG that exploits LLM safety alignment homogeneity by injecting restricted-risk-context documents to induce refusals.

title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
authors: Yuming Xu and Mingtao Zhang and Zhuohan Ge and Haoyang Li and Nicole Hu and Yongqi Zhang and Zhiyuan Wen and Jason Chen Zhang and Qing Li and Lei Chen
actual_contribution: A survey of RAG security organized via the SLOT taxonomy (Surface/Layer/Objective/Target), mapping attacks, defenses, and evaluation benchmarks along the knowledge-access pipeline.

title: DiscourseFlip: An Oblique Discourse-Level Opinion Manipulation Attack against Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yuyang Gong and Miaokun Chen and Jiawei Liu and Zhuo Chen and Guoxiu He and Wei Lu and XiaoFeng Wang and Xiaozhong Liu
actual_contribution: Introduces a discourse-level opinion manipulation threat model against black-box RAG and proposes DiscourseFlip, a graph-guided agentic poisoning attack that propagates stance shifts across semantically related queries.

title: Confundo: Learning to Generate Robust Poison for Practical RAG Systems
authors: Haoyang Hu and Zhejun Jiang and Yueming Lyu and Junyuan Zhang and Yi Liu and Ka-Ho Chow
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning Attacks on RAG
actual_contribution: Proposes Confundo, a fine-tuned LLM-based poison generator that produces robust, stealthy poison texts to attack practical RAG pipelines across multiple objectives (factual manipulation, opinion bias, hallucination).

title: BiRD: A Bidirectional Ranking Defense Mechanism for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Chengcai Gao and Zhihong Sun and Xiaochuan Shi and Qiufeng Wang and Chao Liang
actual_contribution: Proposes BiRD, a defense for RAG that filters poisoned documents by combining forward content relevance with backward ranking consistency, demonstrating reductions in attack success rate against PoisonedRAG and prompt-injection attacks.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
authors: Heydar Soudani and Hamed Zamani and Faegheh Hasibi
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control / Uncertainty in RAG
actual_contribution: Proposes R2C, a consistency-based uncertainty quantification method for retrieval-augmented reasoning that perturbs reasoning paths via query paraphrasing, critical rethinking, and answer validation, improving AUROC and downstream abstention/model selection.

title: Parameters vs. Context: Fine-Grained Control of Knowledge Reliance in Language Models
authors: Baolong Bi and Shenghua Liu and Yiwei Wang and Yilong Xu and Junfeng Fang and Lingrui Mei and Xueqi Cheng
actual_contribution: Proposes CK-PLUG, a plug-and-play decoding-time method that detects parameter-context knowledge conflicts via a Confidence Gain (entropy) metric and modulates token distributions with a tunable parameter to control reliance on parametric vs. contextual knowledge in RAG.

title: Divide-Then-Align: Honest Alignment based on the Knowledge Boundary of RAG
authors: Xin Sun and Jianan Xie and Zhongqi Chen and Qiang Liu and Shu Wu and Yuehe Chen and Bowen Song and Weiqiang Wang and Zilei Wang and Liang Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes Divide-Then-Align (DTA), a DPO-based post-training method that partitions RAG samples into four knowledge-boundary quadrants and teaches models to abstain ('I don't know') when queries fall outside both parametric and retrieval knowledge boundaries.

title: ATM: Adversarial Tuning Multi-agent System Makes a Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generator
authors: Zhu, Junda and Yan, Lingyong and Shi, Haibo and Yin, Dawei and Sha, Lei
actual_contribution: ATM introduces an attacker-generator adversarial tuning loop where an attacker LLM injects fabricated/permuted documents to train a more robust RAG generator that resists noisy and fabricated retrieved content.

title: Understanding Data Poisoning Attacks for RAG: Insights and Algorithms
authors: Xun Xian and Tong Wang and Liwen You and Yanjun Qi
actual_contribution: Analyzes targeted data poisoning attacks on RAG retrieval, showing effective attacks lie along low-variance directions, and proposes a DRS-based defense filter plus a DRS-regularized stealthier attack.

title: When Evidence Conflicts: Uncertainty and Order Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Yikun Han and Mengfei Lan and Halil Kilicoglu
actual_contribution: Evaluates six open-weight LLMs on the HealthContradict biomedical QA benchmark under controlled correct/incorrect/conflicting-order evidence conditions, quantifying accuracy, calibration, and order-induced answer flips, and proposes a conflict-aware abstention score that outperforms confidence-only selective prediction.

title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents
authors: Shrey Shah and Levent Ozgur
actual_contribution: Introduces Synthetic Web Benchmark, a procedurally generated environment for diagnosing how language agents fail under rank-controlled adversarial misinformation injection, with process traces and calibration metrics.

title: Seeing through the Conflict: Transparent Knowledge Conflict Handling in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hua Ye and Siyuan Chen and Ziqi Zhong and Canran Xiao and Haoliang Zhang and Yuhan Wu and Fei Shen
actual_contribution: Proposes TCR, a plug-and-play RAG module that disentangles semantic relevance, factual consistency, and self-answerability into scalar signals fed via soft prompts to detect and resolve context-memory knowledge conflicts.

title: MEMSAD: Gradient-Coupled Anomaly Detection for Memory Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Agents
authors: Ishrith Gowda
actual_contribution: Proposes MEMSAD, a write-time anomaly detection defense against memory-poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented LLM agents, with gradient-coupling theorems, certified detection radius, and minimax-optimal calibration guarantees.

title: LLM-Oriented Information Retrieval: A Denoising-First Perspective
authors: Lu Dai and Liang Sun and Fanpu Cao and Ziyang Rao and Cehao Yang and Hao Liu and Hui Xiong
actual_contribution: A SIGIR'26 perspective/survey paper proposing denoising as the primary objective of LLM-oriented IR, with a pipeline-organized taxonomy spanning indexing, retrieval, context assembly, verification, and agentic loops, covering distractors, knowledge conflicts, and adversarial corruption.

title: Is Conformal Factuality for RAG-based LLMs Robust? Novel Metrics and Systematic Insights
authors: Yi Chen and Daiwei Chen and Sukrut Madhav Chikodikar and Caitlyn Heqi Yin and Ramya Korlakai Vinayak
actual_contribution: Systematically analyzes conformal factuality filtering for RAG-based LLMs, introducing informativeness-aware metrics and showing fragility under distribution shifts/distractors, while comparing entailment vs LLM-based scorers for efficiency.

title: GRACE: Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Response and Abstention under Contextual Evidence
authors: Yibo Zhao and Jiapeng Zhu and Zichen Ding and Xiang Li
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Grounding
actual_contribution: Proposes GRACE, an RL framework with multi-stage gated rewards that trains RAG models to ground answers in cited evidence or explicitly abstain when retrieved context is insufficient.

title: Exploring Knowledge Conflicts for Faithful LLM Reasoning: Benchmark and Method
authors: Tianzhe Zhao and Jiaoyan Chen and Shuxiu Zhang and Haiping Zhu and Qika Lin and Jun Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes ConflictQA, a benchmark for cross-source knowledge conflicts (text vs. KG) in RAG, evaluates 12 LLMs, and introduces XoT, a two-stage explanation-based prompting method to improve faithful reasoning under conflicts.

title: ERA: Evidence-based Reliability Alignment for Honest Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Sunguk Shin and Meeyoung Cha and Byung-Jun Lee and Sungwon Park
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Abstention under Knowledge Conflict
actual_contribution: Proposes ERA, an evidential deep learning framework using Dirichlet distributions and Dempster-Shafer theory to disentangle epistemic/aleatoric uncertainty and quantify knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and retrieved context, enabling calibrated abstention in RAG.

title: Cordon-MAS: Defending RAG against Knowledge Poisoning via Information-Flow Control
authors: Zhe Yu and Wenpeng Xing and Gaolei Li and Shuguang Xiong and Hongzhi Wang and Xuyang Teng and Meng Han
actual_contribution: Introduces CORDON-MAS, a multi-agent defense framework that enforces information-flow separation between untrusted retrieved evidence and the final synthesizer to defend RAG against knowledge poisoning, reducing ASR by 92.4% across five BEIR datasets.

title: Beyond Explicit Refusals: Soft-Failure Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Wentao Zhang and Yan Zhuang and ZhuHang Zheng and Mingfei Zhang and Jiawen Deng and Fuji Ren
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Jamming Attacks
actual_contribution: Formalizes 'soft failure' as a stealthy availability threat to RAG and introduces DEJA, an evolutionary black-box framework that crafts adversarial documents inducing fluent but non-informative answers while evading perplexity-based defenses.

title: Architecture Matters: Comparing RAG Systems under Knowledge Base Poisoning
authors: Samuel Korn
actual_contribution: Benchmarks four RAG architectures (vanilla, agentic, MADAM-RAG, RLM) under N=1 knowledge base poisoning attacks (naive and CorruptRAG-AK) on Natural Questions, showing a ~58pp ASR spread across architectures and introducing a behavioral taxonomy for evaluating contradiction handling.

title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qingying Niu and Yuhao Wang and Ruiyang Ren and Bohui Fang and Wayne Xin Zhao
actual_contribution: Proposes ArbGraph, a pre-generation evidence arbitration framework that decomposes retrieved documents into atomic claims, builds a support/contradiction graph, and iteratively resolves conflicts to improve long-form RAG factuality and robustness to noise.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper's primary focus is knowledge conflict resolution rather than noisy retrieval/context compression per se, though it does address retrieval noise as part of its motivation.

title: Resisting Contextual Interference in RAG via Parametric-Knowledge Reinforcement
authors: Chenyu Lin and Yilin Wen and Du Su and Hexiang Tan and Fei Sun and Muhan Chen and Chenfu Bao and Zhonghou Lyu
actual_contribution: Proposes Knowledgeable-R1, an RL framework with joint PK/CK/RPK sampling and adaptive advantage modulation to balance parametric vs. contextual knowledge use under conflicting or misleading retrieved context.

title: EcoSafeRAG: Efficient Security through Context Analysis in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Ruobing Yao and Yifei Zhang and Shuang Song and Neng Gao and Chenyang Tu
actual_contribution: Proposes EcoSafeRAG, a defense framework that uses sentence-level segmentation and bait-guided contextual diversity clustering to detect and filter poisoned/adversarial documents in RAG without relying on LLM internal knowledge.

title: Disabling Self-Correction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Stealthy Retriever Poisoning
authors: Yanbo Dai and Zhenlan Ji and Zongjie Li and Kuan Li and Shuai Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes DisarmRAG, a stealthy retriever-poisoning attack using contrastive-learning-based model editing and iterative prompt co-optimization to inject malicious instructions that bypass LLM self-correction in RAG systems.

title: CtrlRAG: Black-box Document Poisoning Attacks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Runqi Sui
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning Attacks and Defenses
actual_contribution: Proposes CtrlRAG, a black-box document poisoning attack against RAG using feedback-driven substitution localization and MLM-based perturbations, plus a knowledge-expansion defense.

title: Conflict-Aware Soft Prompting for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Eunseong Choi and June Park and Hyeri Lee and Jongwuk Lee
actual_contribution: Proposes CARE, which trains a context assessor to produce soft memory embeddings via grounded/adversarial soft prompting to mitigate context-memory conflicts in RAG without fine-tuning the base LLM.

title: Bounding Hallucinations: Information-Theoretic Guarantees for RAG Systems via Merlin-Arthur Protocols
authors: Björn Deiseroth and Max Henning Höth and Kristian Kersting and Letitia Parcalabescu
actual_contribution: Introduces a Merlin-Arthur interactive proof training framework for RAG that induces abstention/reject behavior and information-theoretic mutual-information bounds (Explained Information Fraction) between context and answers, without requiring annotated unanswerable samples.

title: Beyond Black-Box Interventions: Latent Probing for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Linfeng Gao and Qinggang Zhang and Baolong Bi and Bo Zeng and Zheng Yuan and Zerui Chen and Zhimin Wei and Shenghua Liu and Linlong Xu and Longyue Wang and Weihua Luo and Jinsong Su
actual_contribution: Proposes ProbeRAG, which uses latent-space probing to detect aligned vs. conflicting knowledge, prunes noisy context, and applies conflict-aware attention fine-tuning to improve RAG faithfulness under knowledge conflicts.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Paper primarily targets knowledge conflict and faithfulness; noise filtering is one of three components.

title: Synchronous Faithfulness Monitoring for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Di Wu and Jia-Chen Gu and Fan Yin and Nanyun Peng and Kai-Wei Chang
actual_contribution: Introduces SynCheck, a lightweight synchronous monitor combining likelihood, uncertainty, context influence, and semantic alignment to detect unfaithful RAG outputs, and FOD, a faithfulness-oriented beam-search decoding algorithm, evaluated on a six-task long-form RAG faithfulness benchmark.

title: On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
authors: Xun Xian and Ganghua Wang and Xuan Bi and Jayanth Srinivasa and Ashish Kundu and Charles Fleming and Mingyi Hong and Jie Ding
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial corruption: poisoning attacks and defenses
actual_contribution: Demonstrates universal poisoning attacks against dense retrievers in RAG for medical/legal QA, explains via an orthogonal augmentation property, and proposes a Mahalanobis-distance detection defense.

title: Revisiting Robust RAG: Do We Still Need Complex Robust Training in the Era of Powerful LLMs?
authors: Ding, Hanxing and Tao, Shuchang and Pang, Liang and Wei, Zihao and Chen, Liwei and Xu, Kun and Shen, Huawei and Cheng, Xueqi
actual_contribution: Empirically shows that as LLM capacity grows, complex robust RAG training (sophisticated document selection, adversarial losses like RAAT/IRM) yields diminishing returns over simple training (e.g., random documents), attributing this to stronger models' inherent calibration, generalization, and attention patterns.

title: After Retrieval, Before Generation: Enhancing the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in RAG
authors: Dai, Xinbang and Hu, Huikang and Hua, Yuncheng and Li, Jiaqi and Hu, Nan and Chen, Yongrui and Jin, Rihui and Zhang, Yuxin and Zhang, Yuyang and Li, Xiaoguang and Shang, Lifeng and Qi, Guilin
actual_contribution: Introduces TRD benchmark covering four RAG scenarios (consistent, internal-faithful, external-faithful, refuse-to-answer) and proposes BRIDGE, a soft-bias allocator with decision tree to dynamically resolve internal/external knowledge conflicts including refusal.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jingxi Qiu and Zeyu Han and Cheng Huang
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Selective RAG
actual_contribution: Proposes SURE-RAG, an aggregation protocol that turns pair-level claim-evidence relation distributions into answer-level sufficiency labels (supported/refuted/insufficient) with a calibrated selective-answering score, evaluated on a controlled HotpotQA-RAG v3 benchmark with risk-coverage and ECE metrics.

title: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Medical Multi-Modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Peiru Yang and Haoran Zheng and Tong Ju and Shiting Wang and Wanchun Ni and Jiajun Liu and Shangguang Wang and Yongfeng Huang and Tao Qi
actual_contribution: Introduces M3Att, a query-agnostic knowledge poisoning attack on medical multimodal RAG that combines distribution-guided retrieval hijacking via PGD-perturbed images with clinical ambiguity-guided misinformation injection in paired texts.

title: BalanceRAG: Joint Risk Calibration for Cascaded Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zijun Jia and Yuanchang Ye and Sen Jia and Yiyao Qian and Haoning Wang and Baojie Chen and Diyin Tang and Jinsong Yu and Zhiyuan Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes BalanceRAG, a training-free joint risk-calibration framework for cascaded LLM-only/RAG routing that uses sequential graphical testing over a threshold lattice to certify operating points with finite-sample selection-conditioned risk control, supporting abstention and multi-risk (retrieval-rate) constraints.

title: The Silent Saboteur: Imperceptible Adversarial Attacks against Black-Box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Song, Hongru and Liu, Yu-An and Zhang, Ruqing and Guo, Jiafeng and Lv, Jianming and de Rijke, Maarten and Cheng, Xueqi
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Retrieval and Poisoning Attacks
actual_contribution: Proposes ReGENT, an RL-based black-box adversarial attack that applies imperceptible word substitutions to a target document so it enters top-k retrieval and manipulates RAG generation, demonstrating high attack success while preserving naturalness.

title: The RAG Paradox: A Black-Box Attack Exploiting Unintentional Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Choi, Chanwoo and Kim, Jinsoo and Cho, Sukmin and Jeong, Soyeong and Chang, Buru
actual_contribution: Proposes PARADOX, a realistic black-box corpus poisoning attack on RAG systems that infers retriever preferences from exposed sources to craft natural-looking poisoned documents.

title: Who Taught the Lie? Responsibility Attribution for Poisoned Knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang and Haoran Xin and Yuxi Chen and Zhuqing Liu and Biao Yi and Tong Li and Lihai Nie and Zheli Liu and Minghong Fang
actual_contribution: Proposes RAGOrigin, a black-box forensic/attribution framework that identifies poisoned texts in a RAG knowledge database responsible for misgeneration events, using adaptive scope selection and a combined retrieval/semantic/generation responsibility score.

title: Topic-FlipRAG: Topic-Orientated Adversarial Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
authors: Yuyang Gong and Zhuo Chen and Jiawei Liu and Miaokun Chen and Fengchang Yu and Wei Lu and Xiaofeng Wang and Xiaozhong Liu
actual_contribution: Introduces Topic-FlipRAG, a black-box topic-oriented adversarial attack that combines LLM knowledge-guided document edits with gradient-based ranking triggers to manipulate stance polarity in RAG outputs across related queries.

title: Resolving Conflicting Evidence in Automated Fact-Checking: A Study on Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
authors: Ziyu Ge and Yuhao Wu and Daniel Wai Kit Chin and Roy Ka-Wei Lee and Rui Cao
actual_contribution: Introduces the CONFACT dataset and evaluates RAG-based LLMs on fact-checking with conflicting evidence from sources of varying credibility, proposing strategies that integrate media source credibility into retrieval/ranking/generation.

title: RAG-Pull: Turning Retrieval into a Code-Injection Channel via Invisible Unicode Perturbations
authors: Aritra Dhar and Vasilije Stambolic and Lukas Cavigelli
actual_contribution: Introduces RAG-PULL, an imperceptible Unicode-perturbation attack on code-RAG pipelines that manipulates queries and/or corpus snippets to steer retrieval toward attacker-controlled vulnerable code, demonstrating transferability across 14 embedders.

title: Poisoned-MRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Yinuo Liu and Zenghui Yuan and Guiyao Tie and Jiawen Shi and Pan Zhou and Lichao Sun and Neil Zhenqiang Gong
actual_contribution: Proposes Poisoned-MRAG, a knowledge poisoning attack on multimodal RAG that injects malicious image-text pairs to manipulate VLM outputs, with both dirty-label and clean-label variants and evaluation of defenses.

title: One Pic is All it Takes: Poisoning Visual Document Retrieval Augmented Generation with a Single Image
authors: Ezzeldin Shereen and Dan Ristea and Shae McFadden and Burak Hasircioglu and Vasilios Mavroudis and Chris Hicks
actual_contribution: Proposes targeted and universal poisoning attacks on visual document RAG systems by injecting a single adversarial image into the KB, using multi-objective PGD optimization, evaluated across white-box and black-box settings and defenses.

title: FlippedRAG: Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Adversarial Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
authors: Zhuo Chen and Yuyang Gong and Jiawei Liu and Miaokun Chen and Haotan Liu and Qikai Cheng and Fan Zhang and Wei Lu and Xiaozhong Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes FlippedRAG, a black-box transfer attack that imitates the RAG retriever to craft poisoning triggers shifting RAG-generated opinions on controversial topics, and evaluates defenses.

title: Faithfulness-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Fact-Checking the Output of Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Ekaterina Fadeeva and Aleksandr Rubashevskii and Dzianis Piatrashyn and Roman Vashurin and Shehzaad Dhuliawala and Artem Shelmanov and Timothy Baldwin and Preslav Nakov and Mrinmaya Sachan and Maxim Panov
actual_contribution: Proposes FRANQ, a faithfulness-aware uncertainty quantification method for RAG outputs with calibration, and introduces a long-form QA dataset annotated for factuality and faithfulness.

title: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection
authors: Tongyu Wen and Chenglong Wang and Xiyuan Yang and Haoyu Tang and Yueqi Xie and Lingjuan Lyu and Zhicheng Dou and Fangzhao Wu
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Introduces a detection-based defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG/LLM systems using hidden states and gradients from intermediate layers as discriminative features.

title: DeRAG: Black-box Adversarial Attacks on Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications via Prompt Injection
authors: Jerry Wang and Fang Yu
actual_contribution: Proposes DeRAG, a gradient-free black-box adversarial attack that uses Differential Evolution to craft short adversarial suffixes that re-rank a target (incorrect) document into top-k retrieval results in RAG pipelines, degrading downstream answer quality.

title: CtrlA: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Inherent Control
authors: Liu, Huanshuo and Zhang, Hao and Guo, Zhijiang and Wang, Jing and Dong, Kuicai and Li, Xiangyang and Lee, Yi Quan and Zhang, Cong and Liu, Yong
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: CtrlA extracts honesty and confidence direction features from LLM representations to steer outputs and monitor confidence, triggering retrieval adaptively when the model is unconfident.

title: ConfRAG: Confidence-Guided Retrieval-Augmenting Generation
authors: Yin Huang and Yifan Ethan Xu and Kai Sun and Vera Yan and Alicia Sun and Haidar Khan and Jimmy Nguyen and Jingxiang Chen and Mohammad Kachuee and Zhaojiang Lin and Yue Liu and Aaron Colak and Anuj Kumar and Wen-tau Yih and Xin Luna Dong
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve and Abstain
actual_contribution: Proposes ConfQA fine-tuning to teach LLMs to abstain on low-confidence factual questions, and ConfRAG which uses these abstentions as a trigger for invoking retrieval, reducing hallucinations and unnecessary retrievals.

title: Chain-of-Thought Poisoning Attacks against R1-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Hongru Song and Yu-an Liu and Ruqing Zhang and Jiafeng Guo and Yixing Fan
actual_contribution: Introduces a knowledge-base poisoning attack that wraps fake knowledge in chain-of-thought reasoning templates to mislead R1-based RAG systems, improving attack success over PoisonedRAG and prompt-hijacking baselines.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice
authors: Quang Hieu Pham and Hoang Ngo and Anh Tuan Luu and Dat Quoc Nguyen
actual_contribution: Introduces WhoQA, a 5K-question benchmark that induces natural knowledge conflicts by asking about shared properties of same-name Wikipedia entities, and shows LLMs degrade and often bias toward popular answers under such conflicts.

title: Unanswerability Evaluation for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Xiangyu Peng and Prafulla Kumar Choubey and Caiming Xiong and Chien-Sheng Wu
benchmark_or_task: Evaluation benchmarks for abstention and unanswerability
actual_contribution: Introduces UAEval4RAG, a framework with a six-category taxonomy of unanswerable requests and an automated pipeline to synthesize them for arbitrary knowledge bases, evaluating RAG systems' abstention/rejection ability via unanswered and acceptable ratios.

title: Studying Large Language Model Behaviors Under Context-Memory Conflicts With Real Documents
authors: Evgenii Kortukov and Alexander Rubinstein and Elisa Nguyen and Seong Joon Oh
actual_contribution: Introduces a realistic framework for studying context-memory knowledge conflicts using real factual documents that contradict the model's incorrect parametric answers, finding that LLMs usually update but exhibit a 'parametric bias' where an incorrect parametric answer appearing in context increases update failure.

title: RetrievalQA: Assessing Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Short-form Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Zihan Zhang and Meng Fang and Ling Chen
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and control: when to retrieve
actual_contribution: Introduces RetrievalQA, a 1,271-question benchmark covering new-world and long-tail knowledge to evaluate adaptive RAG methods, and proposes TA-ARE, an ICL-based calibration-free adaptive retrieval method.

title: Rag and Roll: An End-to-End Evaluation of Indirect Prompt Manipulations in LLM-based Application Frameworks
authors: Gianluca De Stefano and Lea Schönherr and Giancarlo Pellegrino
actual_contribution: Presents Rag-n-Roll, an end-to-end evaluation framework testing indirect prompt injection / corpus poisoning attacks against various RAG configurations, finding existing ranking-focused attacks plateau around 40% success.

title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
authors: Tianjun Zhang and Shishir G. Patil and Naman Jain and Sheng Shen and Matei Zaharia and Ion Stoica and Joseph E. Gonzalez
actual_contribution: RAFT is a fine-tuning recipe for domain-specific RAG that trains LLMs with a mix of golden and distractor documents and chain-of-thought answers quoting source spans, improving robustness to irrelevant retrieved context.
limitation_or_note: citation/grounding paragraph: RAFT does train models to quote source spans verbatim, so the claim partially matches; however RAFT is not really a 'grounding method' for claim-level citation verification but a domain-specific RAG fine-tuning recipe.

title: Poisoned LangChain: Jailbreak LLMs by LangChain
authors: Ziqiu Wang and Jun Liu and Shengkai Zhang and Yang Yang
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Introduces Poisoned-LangChain, an indirect jailbreak attack on LLMs via RAG by injecting disguised malicious content into the external knowledge base, triggered by keywords, achieving high attack success rates on six Chinese LLMs.

title: Neural Exec: Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Dario Pasquini and Martin Strohmeier and Carmela Troncoso
actual_contribution: Proposes optimization-based generation of prompt-injection execution triggers (Neural Exec) that persist through RAG preprocessing pipelines, achieving high attack success rates against open-source LLMs.

title: Cutting Off the Head Ends the Conflict: A Mechanism for Interpreting and Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
authors: Zhuoran Jin and Pengfei Cao and Hongbang Yuan and Yubo Chen and Jiexin Xu and Huaijun Li and Xiaojian Jiang and Kang Liu and Jun Zhao
actual_contribution: Identifies memory heads and context heads in later transformer layers as the pivotal point where knowledge conflicts emerge, and proposes PH3 (pruning heads via path patching) to flexibly steer LMs toward internal memory or external context.

title: Backdoored Retrievers for Prompt Injection Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Cody Clop and Yannick Teglia
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Retriever Backdoors and Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Investigates prompt injection attacks against RAG via corpus poisoning and backdoored dense retrievers, demonstrating high attack success rates for malicious link insertion, advertising, and denial-of-service objectives across multiple LLMs.

title: Tricking Retrievers with Influential Tokens: An Efficient Black-Box Corpus Poisoning Attack
authors: Cheng Wang and Yiwei Wang and Yujun Cai and Bryan Hooi
actual_contribution: Proposes DIGA, a black-box genetic-algorithm corpus poisoning attack that exploits retrievers' token-order insensitivity and bias towards influential tokens to craft adversarial passages efficiently.

title: Token-Level Precise Attack on RAG: Searching for the Best Alternatives to Mislead Generation
authors: Li, Zizhong and Zhang, Haopeng and Zhang, Jiawei
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption / Poisoning Attacks on RAG
actual_contribution: Introduces TPARAG, a token-level adversarial attack framework that uses a lightweight white-box LLM to craft malicious passages targeting both retrieval and generation in RAG systems under black- and white-box settings.

title: RIPRAG: Hack a Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Question-Answering System with Reinforcement Learning
authors: Meng Xi and Sihan Lv and Yechen Jin and Guanjie Cheng and Naibo Wang and Ying Li and Jianwei Yin
actual_contribution: Introduces RIPRAG, an RL-based black-box poisoning attack against RAG QA systems, using black-box feedback (RLBF) and a novel BRPO algorithm to generate adversarial documents that achieve high attack success rates even against defended systems.

title: RAG Safety: Exploring Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Tianzhe Zhao and Jiaoyan Chen and Yanchi Ru and Haiping Zhu and Nan Hu and Jun Liu and Qika Lin
actual_contribution: Proposes a black-box data poisoning attack on KG-based RAG systems that injects perturbation triples to complete misleading inference chains, demonstrating substantial QA degradation across four KG-RAG methods on WebQSP and CWQ.

title: One shot dominance: Knowledge poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented generation systems
authors: Zhiyuan Chang and Mingyang Li and Xiaojun Jia and Junjie Wang and Yuekai Huang and Ziyou Jiang and Yang Liu and Qing Wang
actual_contribution: Introduces AuthChain, a knowledge poisoning attack that injects a single authoritative, evidence-chain-structured poisoned document into a RAG knowledge base to manipulate LLM outputs even for multi-hop queries, evading existing RAG defenses.

title: MM-PoisonRAG: Disrupting Multimodal RAG with Local and Global Poisoning Attacks
authors: Hyeonjeong Ha and Qiusi Zhan and Jeonghwan Kim and Dimitrios Bralios and Saikrishna Sanniboina and Nanyun Peng and Kai-Wei Chang and Daniel Kang and Heng Ji
actual_contribution: Introduces MM-PoisonRAG, a framework with localized and globalized poisoning attacks on multimodal RAG showing high attack success and ineffective defenses.

title: Hoist with His Own Petard: Inducing Guardrails to Facilitate Denial-of-Service Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLMs
authors: Suo, Pan and Shang, Yu-Ming and Guo, San-Chuan and Zhang, Xi
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Injection Attacks
actual_contribution: Introduces MutedRAG, a denial-of-service attack on RAG that injects minimal jailbreak prompts into the corpus to weaponize LLM safety guardrails into refusing legitimate queries.

title: A Few Words Can Distort Graphs: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Jiayi Wen and Tianxin Chen and Zhirun Zheng and Cheng Huang
actual_contribution: Introduces two knowledge poisoning attacks (targeted TKPA and universal UKPA) against GraphRAG that modify a tiny fraction of source text to distort the constructed knowledge graph and evade existing defenses.

title: Traceback of Poisoned Texts in Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang and Haoran Xin and Minghong Fang and Zhuqing Liu and Biao Yi and Tong Li and Zheli Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes RAGForensics, a post-hoc traceback system that identifies poisoned texts in a RAG knowledge database from user feedback on incorrect outputs, evaluated against PoisonedRAG and instruction injection attacks.

title: RevPRAG: Revealing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation through LLM Activation Analysis
authors: Tan, Xue and Luan, Hao and Luo, Mingyu and Sun, Xiaoyan and Chen, Ping and Dai, Jun
actual_contribution: RevPRAG detects RAG poisoning attacks by analyzing distinct activation patterns of LLMs when generating correct vs. poisoned responses, achieving ~98% TPR and ~1% FPR across multiple LLMs and retrievers.

title: Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
authors: Wang, Yike and Feng, Shangbin and Wang, Heng and Shi, Weijia and Balachandran, Vidhisha and He, Tianxing and Tsvetkov, Yulia
actual_contribution: Proposes an evaluation framework and instruction-based methods for detecting and resolving knowledge conflicts between LLM parametric knowledge and contextual information, across three tasks of increasing difficulty.

title: Beyond RAG vs. Long-Context: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Knowledge Grounding
authors: Seongwoong Shim and Myunsoo Kim and Jae Hyeon Cho and Byung-Jun Lee
actual_contribution: Proposes LDAR, a lightweight learned retriever that selects passages from a similarity quantile band to balance information coverage and distraction, outperforming RAG and long-context approaches with lower token usage.

title: Whose Facts Win? LLM Source Preferences under Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Jakob Schuster and Vagrant Gautam and Katja Markert
actual_contribution: Introduces a synthetic-source, synthetic-conflict evaluation framework to measure LLM source preferences under inter-context knowledge conflicts across 13 open models, finds a consistent credibility hierarchy that can be flipped by repetition, and proposes a fine-tuning method to mitigate repetition bias.

title: Towards Unsupervised Adversarial Document Detection in Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Patrick Levi
actual_contribution: A preliminary unsupervised method to detect adversarial documents in RAG by treating generator activations, output embeddings, and TokenSAR entropy as outlier indicators via Grubbs' test.

title: Towards Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Review of Threats, Defenses and Benchmarks
authors: Yanming Mu and Hao Hu and Feiyang Li and Qiao Yuan and Jiang Wu and Zichuan Liu and Pengcheng Liu and Mei Wang and Hongwei Zhou and Yuling Liu
actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of RAG security threats (poisoning, MIA, adversarial, embedding inversion, indirect injection), defenses (encryption, DP, federated learning, sanitization), and evaluation benchmarks.

title: Towards Dependable Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Factual Confidence Prediction
authors: Florian Geissler and Francesco Carella and Laura Fieback and Jakob Spiegelberg
actual_contribution: Proposes a two-stage RAG dependability pipeline: conformal prediction for retrieval chunk filtering with statistical guarantees, plus an attention-based (lookback ratio) classifier for hallucination/factuality detection.

title: The Curse of Helpfulness: Inverse Scaling Law in Robustness to Distractor Instructions via DistractionIF
authors: Zeli Su and Zhankai Xu and Tianlei Chen and Longfei Zheng and Xiaolu Zhang and Jun Zhou and Wentao Zhang
actual_contribution: Proposes DistractionIF, a benchmark measuring LLM robustness to benign instruction-like noise embedded in reference text, reveals an inverse scaling phenomenon, and shows GRPO can restore robustness.

title: RefineRAG: Word-Level Poisoning Attacks via Retriever-Guided Text Refinement
authors: Ziye Wang and Guanyu Wang and Kailong Wang
actual_contribution: Introduces RefineRAG, a two-stage poisoning attack on RAG that combines macro seed generation with retriever-guided word-level MLM refinement, achieving high ASR with low perplexity and strong transferability.

title: RedVisor: Reasoning-Aware Prompt Injection Defense via Zero-Copy KV Cache Reuse
authors: Mingrui Liu and Sixiao Zhang and Cheng Long and Kwok-Yan Lam
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Proposes RedVisor, a two-phase prompt injection defense using a top-layer gated adapter for explainable injection detection followed by guided generation, with zero-copy KV cache reuse for efficient deployment.

title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Haozhen Wang and Haoyue Liu and Jionghao Zhu and Zhichao Wang and Yongxin Guo and Xiaoying Tang
actual_contribution: Proposes PIDP-Attack, a compound RAG attack combining query-time prompt injection with corpus poisoning that misleads LLMs without prior knowledge of user queries.

title: Neuro-RIT: Neuron-Guided Instruction Tuning for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Language Model
authors: Jaemin Kim and Jae O Lee and Sumyeong Ahn and Seo Yeon Park
actual_contribution: Neuro-RIT identifies relevant vs. irrelevant context-aware neurons via attribution and applies two-stage instruction tuning to suppress noise-aware neurons while reinforcing evidence distillation, improving RALM robustness to noisy retrieval.

title: MTRAG-UN: A Benchmark for Open Challenges in Multi-Turn RAG Conversations
authors: Sara Rosenthal and Yannis Katsis and Vraj Shah and Lihong He and Lucian Popa and Marina Danilevsky
benchmark_or_task: Evaluation/benchmarks for OOD, abstention, and clarification
actual_contribution: MTRAG-UN is a 666-task multi-turn RAG benchmark spanning 6 domains, focusing on unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone questions and clarification responses, with retrieval and generation evaluations showing frontier LLMs struggle with these cases.

title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs
authors: Junhyeok Lee and Han Jang and Kyu Sung Choi
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial corruption: indirect prompt injection benchmarks
actual_contribution: Introduces MPIB, a benchmark of 9,697 instances for evaluating direct and RAG-mediated prompt injection attacks on LLMs in clinical settings, with a clinical harm taxonomy and outcome-based CHER metric alongside ASR.

title: Lost in the Evidence? Reproducing Document Position and Context Size Effects in RAG
authors: Jorge Gabín and Anxo Perez and Javier Parapar
actual_contribution: Reproducibility study of positional bias (lost-in-the-middle) and context size effects in RAG, introducing a topic-budget calibration procedure and analyzing interactions among retrieval quality, ordering, context size, and model scale.

title: LogicPoison: Logical Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
