authors: Yilin Xiao and Jin Chen and Qinggang Zhang and Yujing Zhang and Chuang Zhou and Longhao Yang and Lingfei Ren and Xin Yang and Xiao Huang
actual_contribution: Proposes LogicPoison, a topology-targeted attack on GraphRAG that uses type-preserving entity swapping to corrupt knowledge graph logical reasoning chains while evading content-based defenses.

title: KEPo: Knowledge Evolution Poison on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qizhi Chen and Chao Qi and Yihong Huang and Muquan Li and Rongzheng Wang and Dongyang Zhang and Ke Qin and Shuang Liang
actual_contribution: Introduces KEPo, a knowledge-evolution-based poisoning attack against graph-based RAG that forges evolution paths to inject malicious facts into the KG, achieving SOTA attack success rates.

title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
authors: Alexandra Bazarova and Andrei Volodichev and Daria Kotova and Alexey Zaytsev
actual_contribution: Proposes INTRYGUE, an induction-head-aware gating of predictive entropy for uncertainty quantification in RAG, addressing entropy-neuron-induced false uncertainty.

title: How Large Language Models Balance Internal Knowledge with User and Document Assertions
authors: Shuowei Li and Haoxin Li and Wenda Chu and Yi Fang
actual_contribution: Introduces a three-source (parametric/user/document) interaction evaluation framework and benchmarks 27 LLMs, revealing document-preference bias and limited discrimination of helpful vs. harmful external context, with SFT-based mitigation.

title: Hidden-in-Plain-Text: A Benchmark for Social-Web Indirect Prompt Injection in RAG
authors: Haoze Guo and Ziqi Wei
actual_contribution: Proposes OpenRAG-Soc, a benchmark and harness for evaluating indirect prompt injection and retrieval poisoning attacks on web-facing RAG systems, with deployable defenses (sanitization, normalization, attribution-gated prompting).

title: Hidden in the Metadata: Stealth Poisoning Attacks on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kennedy Edemacu and Mohammad Mahdi Shokri
actual_contribution: Introduces MM-MEPA, a metadata-only poisoning attack on multimodal RAG that modifies textual metadata via constrained optimization to manipulate retrieval and generation while evading consistency-check defenses.

title: Grounded Decoding: Retrieval-Anchored Probability Fusion for Faithful RAG
authors: Ibne Farabi Shihab and Fariya Afrin and Sanjeda Akter and Anuj Sharma
actual_contribution: Introduces Grounded Decoding, a training-free decoding-time method that fuses full-RAG and retrieval-only next-token distributions via a KL-barycenter objective with adaptive weighting based on distributional conflict and retriever trust, improving factuality and citation quality.

title: Generating Leakage-Free Benchmarks for Robust RAG Evaluation
authors: Jiayi Liu and Jiaxing Zhang and Bowen Jin and Jennifer Neville
actual_contribution: Proposes SeedRG, a pipeline that regenerates multi-hop RAG benchmarks via reasoning-graph extraction and type-constrained entity replacement to reduce knowledge leakage and preserve reasoning difficulty, enabling more discriminative RAG evaluation.

title: Faithfulness-QA: A Counterfactual Entity Substitution Dataset for Training Context-Faithful RAG Models
authors: Li Ju and Junzhe Wang and Qi Zhang
actual_contribution: Constructs a 99K-sample dataset by counterfactual NER-based entity substitution over SQuAD/TriviaQA to create controlled context-memory knowledge conflicts for training and evaluating context-faithful RAG models.

title: Decide Then Retrieve: A Training-Free Framework with Uncertainty-Guided Triggering and Dual-Path Retrieval
authors: Wang Chen and Guanqiang Qi and Weikang Li and Yang Li and Deguo Xia and Jizhou Huang
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes DTR, a training-free RAG framework that uses LLM generation uncertainty (negative log-likelihood) to decide whether to trigger retrieval, combined with a dual-path retrieval mechanism using both query and pseudo-context for adaptive evidence selection.

title: Can Small Language Models Use What They Retrieve? An Empirical Study of Retrieval Utilization Across Model Scale
authors: Sanchit Pandey
actual_contribution: Empirical study showing that sub-7B LMs fail to utilize retrieved context even under oracle retrieval, and that adding any context (including oracle) destroys parametric knowledge — a distraction effect that dominates over retrieval quality.

title: CODE: A Contradiction-Based Deliberation Extension Framework for Overthinking Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Xiaolei Zhang and Xiaojun Jia and Liquan Chen and Songze Li
actual_contribution: Introduces CODE, a multi-agent knowledge-base poisoning attack on RAG systems that crafts contradiction-laden retrievable documents to inflate reasoning-token consumption of reasoning LLMs without degrading answer accuracy.

title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
authors: Md Jahedur Rahman and Ihsen Alouani
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
actual_contribution: Proposes a GCG-based universal adversarial suffix that evades activation-based task-drift detectors for prompt injection, and a suffix-augmentation defense.

title: Benchmarking Knowledge-Extraction Attack and Defense on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhisheng Qi and Utkarsh Sahu and Li Ma and Haoyu Han and Ryan Rossi and Franck Dernoncourt and Mahantesh Halappanavar and Nesreen Ahmed and Yushun Dong and Yue Zhao and Yu Zhang and Yu Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes a unified benchmark and design space for evaluating knowledge-extraction attacks and defenses on RAG systems across multiple datasets, retrievers, generators, and defense strategies.

title: Adversarial Hubness Detector: Detecting Hubness Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Idan Habler and Vineeth Sai Narajala and Stav Koren and Amy Chang and Tiffany Saade
actual_contribution: Proposes a multi-detector open-source scanner that uses robust statistics, cluster spread, stability, and domain/modality-aware analyses to detect adversarial hub poisoning in RAG vector databases.

title: Adaptive Stopping for Multi-Turn LLM Reasoning
authors: Xiaofan Zhou and Huy Nguyen and Bo Yu and Chenxi Liu and Lu Cheng
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and control: when to retrieve and abstain
actual_contribution: Introduces MiCP, a conformal prediction framework for multi-turn LLM reasoning (adaptive RAG, ReAct) that allocates error budgets across turns to enable adaptive early stopping with coverage guarantees and an abstention option.

title: ALDEN: Boosting Private Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Active Learning and Distribution Estimation
authors: Xingyu Lyu and Jianfeng He and Ning Wang and Yidan Hu and Tao Li and Danjue Chen and Shixiong Li and Yimin Chen
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
actual_contribution: Proposes ALDEN, a black-box query-based attack on RAG systems that uses active learning (k-center) and decay-based topic distribution estimation to generate diverse malicious queries that extract more private chunks from the knowledge base than prior prompt-injection/extraction attacks.
limitation_or_note: Adversarial corruption and security.: Paper is primarily a privacy/data-extraction attack rather than corpus poisoning, but fits the broader security/adversarial category.

title: A Sentence Relation-Based Approach to Sanitizing Malicious Instructions
authors: Soumil Datta and Melissa Umble and Daniel S. Brown and Guanhong Tao
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Proposes SONAR, a sentence-level NLI-based sanitization defense that detects and prunes indirect prompt injection content from retrieved context in RAG/agent pipelines.

title: Your RAG is Unfair: Exposing Fairness Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoor Attacks
authors: Bagwe, Gaurav and Chaturvedi, Saket S. and Ma, Xiaolong and Yuan, Xiaoyong and Wang, Kuang-Ching and Zhang, Lan
actual_contribution: Proposes BiasRAG, a two-phase backdoor attack on RAG that poisons the query encoder during pretraining and injects adversarial documents post-deployment to induce fairness-targeted biased outputs while preserving utility.

title: TruthfulRAG: Resolving Factual-level Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs
authors: Shuyi Liu and Yuming Shang and Xi Zhang
actual_contribution: Proposes TruthfulRAG, a KG-based framework that extracts triples from retrieved content, performs query-aware graph retrieval, and uses entropy-based filtering to detect/resolve factual conflicts between parametric and external knowledge in RAG.

title: The Semantic Illusion: Certified Limits of Embedding-Based Hallucination Detection in RAG Systems
authors: Debu Sinha
actual_contribution: Applies split conformal prediction to RAG hallucination detection, showing that embedding/NLI-based detectors fail catastrophically (100% FPR at 95% recall) on real RLHF-aligned hallucinations while LLM judges succeed, demonstrating limits of semantic-similarity-based calibration.

title: The Hidden Threat in Plain Text: Attacking RAG Data Loaders
authors: Alberto Castagnaro and Umberto Salviati and Mauro Conti and Luca Pajola and Simeone Pizzi
actual_contribution: Introduces stealthy document-level poisoning attacks (invisible characters, hidden text, font tricks) targeting RAG data loaders, with a toolkit (PhantomText) demonstrating high ASR across loaders and end-to-end RAG systems.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: Winnowing Down Divergent Views in Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Song Wang and Zihan Chen and Peng Wang and Zhepei Wei and Zhen Tan and Yu Meng and Cong Shen and Jundong Li
actual_contribution: Proposes WinnowRAG, a training-free multi-agent RAG framework that clusters retrieved documents and uses a critic LLM to iteratively filter out noisy ones while retaining useful content.

title: Search Wisely: Mitigating Sub-optimal Agentic Searches By Reducing Uncertainty
authors: Peilin Wu and Mian Zhang and Xinlu Zhang and Xinya Du and Zhiyu Zoey Chen
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Defines over-search and under-search in agentic RAG, links them to model uncertainty about knowledge boundaries, and proposes β-GRPO, a confidence-thresholded RL reward that improves agentic search decisions.

title: SciRerankBench: Benchmarking Rerankers Towards Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated LLMs
authors: Haotian Chen and Qingqing Long and Meng Xiao and Xiao Luo and Wei Ju and Chengrui Wang and Xuezhi Wang and Yuanchun Zhou and Hengshu Zhu
actual_contribution: SciRerankBench is a scientific RAG benchmark with three context-perturbation tasks (noisy, semantically similar-but-irrelevant, counterfactual) to evaluate 13 rerankers across 11 LLMs.

title: SUGAR: Leveraging Contextual Confidence for Smarter Retrieval
authors: Hanna Zubkova and Ji-Hoon Park and Seong-Whan Lee
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes SUGAR, which uses semantic entropy as an uncertainty signal to adaptively choose between no retrieval, single-step, or multi-step retrieval in open-domain QA.

title: RoseRAG: Robust Retrieval-augmented Generation with Small-scale LLMs via Margin-aware Preference Optimization
authors: Tianci Liu and Haoxiang Jiang and Tianze Wang and Ran Xu and Yue Yu and Linjun Zhang and Tuo Zhao and Haoyu Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes RoseRAG, a framework training small-scale LLMs with margin-aware preference optimization (rejection sampling + contrastive preference selection) to make RAG robust to noisy/irrelevant retrieved documents.

title: Robustness via Referencing: Defending against Prompt Injection Attacks by Referencing the Executed Instruction
authors: Yulin Chen and Haoran Li and Yuan Sui and Yue Liu and Yufei He and Xiaoling Bai and Chi Fei and Yabo Li and Haozhe Ma and Yangqiu Song and Bryan Hooi
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Proposes a prompt-engineering defense against direct and indirect prompt injection attacks that asks LLMs to tag each executed instruction with a reference, then filters out responses whose tags don't match the original input instruction.

title: RobustMask: Certified Robustness against Adversarial Neural Ranking Attack via Randomized Masking
authors: Jiawei Liu and Zhuo Chen and Rui Zhu and Miaokun Chen and Yuyang Gong and Wei Lu and Xiaofeng Wang
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial corruption: retrieval attacks and defenses
actual_contribution: Introduces RobustMask, a randomized-masking smoothing defense providing certified top-K robustness for neural ranking models against adversarial perturbations, with applications to RAG retrieval security.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
authors: Chaitanya Sharma
actual_contribution: A comprehensive survey of RAG architectures (retriever/generator/hybrid/robustness), enhancements, evaluation frameworks, and benchmarks, with comparative performance analyses.

title: Retrieval as a Decision: Training-Free Adaptive Gating for Efficient RAG
authors: Yufeng Wang and Lu wei and Haibin Ling
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes TARG, a training-free single-shot gate that uses prefix-logit uncertainty signals (entropy, top-1/top-2 margin, small-N variance) to decide whether RAG retrieval is needed, calibrated via threshold/quantile to a retrieval budget.

title: Rethinking All Evidence: Enhancing Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Conflict-Driven Summarization
authors: Juan Chen and Baolong Bi and Wei Zhang and Jingyan Sui and Xiaofei Zhu and Yuanzhuo Wang and Lingrui Mei and Shenghua Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes CARE-RAG, a framework that elicits diverse parametric evidence, refines retrieved passages to remove noise, and uses a distilled LLaMA-3.2-3B conflict detector to summarize conflicts between internal and external knowledge before answering.
limitation_or_note: Noisy retrieval, distraction, and context compression.: Primary focus is knowledge conflict resolution; noisy retrieval handling is a secondary aspect via context refinement.

title: Reasoning-Style Poisoning of LLM Agents via Stealthy Style Transfer: Process-Level Attacks and Runtime Monitoring in RSV Space
authors: Xingfu Zhou and Pengfei Wang
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Introduces Reasoning-Style Poisoning of LLM agents via stealthy style transfer of retrieved documents, with a Reasoning Style Vector metric and a runtime monitor (RSP-M) that detects style-induced reasoning loops or premature convergence.
limitation_or_note: Adversarial corruption and security: Paper also fits calibration_control via RSP-M runtime monitor, consistent with assigned categories.

title: RPO: Retrieval Preference Optimization for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Shi-Qi Yan and Quan Liu and Zhen-Hua Ling
actual_contribution: Proposes Retrieval Preference Optimization (RPO), a DPO-variant alignment method that integrates retrieval-relevance reward into preference optimization, enabling LLMs to adaptively choose between parametric and retrieved knowledge under conflict.

title: RAGRank: Using PageRank to Counter Poisoning in CTI LLM Pipelines
authors: Austin Jia and Avaneesh Ramesh and Zain Shamsi and Daniel Zhang and Alex Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes RAGRank, a PageRank-derived source credibility score over document/citation graphs to defend RAG (especially CTI) systems against poisoning attacks, demonstrated on MS MARCO and CTI case studies.

title: Query-Level Uncertainty in Large Language Models
authors: Lihu Chen and Gerard de Melo and Fabian M. Suchanek and Gaël Varoquaux
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Introduces a training-free query-level uncertainty estimator (Internal Confidence) using cross-layer/token self-evaluation probabilities, and applies it to adaptive RAG invocation and model cascading.

title: Quantifying and Improving the Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Against Spurious Features in Grounding Data
authors: Shiping Yang and Jie Wu and Wenbiao Ding and Ning Wu and Shining Liang and Ming Gong and Hongzhi Li and Hengyuan Zhang and Angel X. Chang and Dongmei Zhang
actual_contribution: Introduces SURE, a framework with taxonomy, data synthesis pipeline, and instance-level metrics for evaluating and mitigating RALM robustness against spurious (semantic-agnostic) features like format, style, and metadata in retrieved documents.

title: PrismRAG: Boosting RAG Factuality with Distractor Resilience and Strategized Reasoning
authors: Mohammad Kachuee and Teja Gollapudi and Minseok Kim and Yin Huang and Kai Sun and Xiao Yang and Jiaqi Wang and Nirav Shah and Yue Liu and Aaron Colak and Anuj Kumar and Wen-tau Yih and Xin Luna Dong
actual_contribution: PrismRAG fine-tunes LLMs with synthetically generated distractor passages and strategized chain-of-thought reasoning to improve RAG factuality against semi-relevant retrieved noise.

title: Principled Context Engineering for RAG: Statistical Guarantees via Conformal Prediction

title: Parallel Key-Value Cache Fusion for Position Invariant RAG
authors: Philhoon Oh and Jinwoo Shin and James Thorne

title: PRGB Benchmark: A Robust Placeholder-Assisted Algorithm for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhehao Tan and Yihan Jiao and Dan Yang and Lei Liu and Jie Feng and Duolin Sun and Yue Shen and Jian Wang and Peng Wei and Jinjie Gu
actual_contribution: PRGB is a placeholder-based RAG benchmark evaluating LLM document utilization across multi-level noise filtering, combination, and reference reasoning, using placeholder substitution to disentangle parametric vs retrieved knowledge.

title: Noise-Robust Abstractive Compression in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Singon Kim

title: NeuroGenPoisoning: Neuron-Guided Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLM via Genetic Optimization of External Knowledge
authors: Hanyu Zhu and Lance Fiondella and Jiawei Yuan and Kai Zeng and Long Jiao
actual_contribution: Introduces a neuron-attribution + genetic-algorithm framework that crafts adversarial external passages activating 'Poison-Responsive Neurons' to override LLM parametric memory in RAG, achieving >90% population overwrite success across multiple LLMs and QA datasets.

title: Modeling Uncertainty Trends for Timely Retrieval in Dynamic RAG
authors: Bo Li and Tian Tian and Zhenghua Xu and Hao Cheng and Shikun Zhang and Wei Ye

title: Micro-Act: Mitigating Knowledge Conflict in LLM-based RAG via Actionable Self-Reasoning
authors: Nan Huo and Jinyang Li and Bowen Qin and Ge Qu and Xiaolong Li and Xiaodong Li and Chenhao Ma and Reynold Cheng

title: MemoryGraft: Persistent Compromise of LLM Agents via Poisoned Experience Retrieval
authors: Saksham Sahai Srivastava and Haoyu He
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial corruption: poisoning and memory attacks

title: Medusa: Cross-Modal Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Multimodal Medical Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yingjia Shang and Yi Liu and Huimin Wang and Furong Li and Wenfang Sun and Wu Chengyu and Yefeng Zheng

title: LLMail-Inject: A Dataset from a Realistic Adaptive Prompt Injection Challenge
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi and Aideen Fay and Ahmed Salem and Egor Zverev and Kai-Chieh Liao and Chi-Huang Liu and Chun-Chih Kuo and Jannis Weigend and Danyael Manlangit and Alex Apostolov and Haris Umair and João Donato and Masayuki Kawakita and Athar Mahboob and Tran Huu Bach and Tsun-Han Chiang and Myeongjin Cho and Hajin Choi and Byeonghyeon Kim and Hyeonjin Lee and Benjamin Pannell and Conor McCauley and Mark Russinovich and Andrew Paverd and Giovanni Cherubin
actual_contribution: Presents the LLMail-Inject challenge and resulting dataset of adaptive indirect prompt injection attacks against an LLM-based email assistant, evaluating multiple defenses across LLMs and retrieval setups.

title: LLM-Independent Adaptive RAG: Let the Question Speak for Itself
authors: Maria Marina and Nikolay Ivanov and Sergey Pletenev and Mikhail Salnikov and Daria Galimzianova and Nikita Krayko and Vasily Konovalov and Alexander Panchenko and Viktor Moskvoretskii
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes 27 lightweight external features (entity popularity, question type/complexity, context relevance, etc.) for adaptive retrieval decisions, matching uncertainty-based methods at much lower compute.

title: Know Or Not: a library for evaluating out-of-knowledge base robustness
authors: Jessica Foo and Pradyumna Shyama Prasad and Shaun Khoo
actual_contribution: Introduces knowornot, an open-source library and leave-one-out methodology for evaluating LLM abstention/OOKB robustness in RAG, plus PolicyBench benchmark across four policy QA domains.

title: Investigating Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems on Unanswerable, Uncheatable, Realistic, Multi-hop Queries
authors: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu and Bryan Li and Arman Cohan and William Gantt Walden and Eugene Yang
actual_contribution: Introduces CRUMQs, an automatic pipeline for creating difficulty-controlled, uncheatable, unanswerable multi-hop RAG benchmark queries, and evaluates leading RAG systems' abstention behavior.

title: ImportSnare: Directed "Code Manual" Hijacking in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors: Kai Ye and Liangcai Su and Chenxiong Qian
actual_contribution: Introduces ImportSnare, a RAG poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented code generation that injects ranking and inducing sequences into documentation to make LLMs recommend malicious package dependencies.

authors: Kaiwen Zuo and Zelin Liu and Raman Dutt and Ziyang Wang and Zhongtian Sun and Fan Mo and Pietro Liò
actual_contribution: Introduces MedThreatRAG, a multimodal poisoning attack framework (textual, visual, cross-modal conflict injection) targeting medical RAG pipelines, evaluated on IU-Xray and MIMIC-CXR.

title: Exploring the Security Threats of Retriever Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors: Tian Li and Bo Lin and Shangwen Wang and Yusong Tan
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Retrieval Attacks and Backdoors
actual_contribution: Introduces VenomRACG, a stealthy and effective retriever backdoor attack for RACG that injects vulnerability-aware triggers, evades existing defenses, and induces LLMs to generate vulnerable code with <0.05% knowledge base poisoning.

title: Exploring the Security Threats of Knowledge Base Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation
authors: Bo Lin and Shangwen Wang and Liqian Chen and Xiaoguang Mao
actual_contribution: Studies knowledge base poisoning attacks against retrieval-augmented code generation, showing that injecting vulnerable code examples causes LLMs to generate insecure code at high rates.

title: Energy Landscapes Enable Reliable Abstention in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Healthcare
authors: Ravi Shankar and Sheng Wong and Lin Li and Magdalena Bachmann and Alex Silverthorne and Beth Albert and Gabriel Davis Jones
actual_contribution: Proposes an energy-based model trained over dense embeddings to enable reliable abstention in retrieval-augmented LLMs for women's health, outperforming softmax and kNN baselines on hard near-distribution OOD queries.

title: EmoRAG: Evaluating RAG Robustness to Symbolic Perturbations
authors: Xinyun Zhou and Xinfeng Li and Yinan Peng and Ming Xu and Xuanwang Zhang and Miao Yu and Yidong Wang and Xiaojun Jia and Kun Wang and Qingsong Wen and XiaoFeng Wang and Wei Dong
actual_contribution: Demonstrates that injecting emoticons into queries and corpus documents can near-deterministically hijack RAG retrieval, evaluates the vulnerability across retrievers/generators/datasets, and proposes detection-based defenses.

title: END: Early Noise Dropping for Efficient and Effective Context Denoising
authors: Hongye Jin and Pei Chen and Jingfeng Yang and Zhengyang Wang and Fangran Mo and Jinghan Zhang and Meng Jiang and Yifan Gao and Binxuan Huang and Xinyang Zhang and Zheng Li and Tianyi Liu and Huasheng Li and Bing Yin
actual_contribution: Proposes END, an early-layer linear probing method that detects and drops noisy chunks before full LLM forward pass, reducing distraction and computation in RAG/long-context QA.

title: Dynamic Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Mitigating Distractors and Positional Bias
authors: Malika Iratni and Mohand Boughanem and Taoufiq Dkaki
actual_contribution: Empirically analyzes distractor and positional ('lost in the middle') effects in RAG, and proposes a query-specific classifier predicting optimal k combined with LLM reranking to dynamically select context.

title: Do Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Adapt to Varying User Needs?
authors: Peilin Wu and Xinlu Zhang and Wenhao Yu and Xingyu Liu and Xinya Du and Zhiyu Zoey Chen
actual_contribution: Introduces an evaluation framework (and synthetic URAQ dataset) testing RALMs under three user-need instructions crossed with context matching/conflict/irrelevance, showing model-family-dependent trade-offs between context faithfulness and memory reliance.

title: Defending Against Knowledge Poisoning Attacks During Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kennedy Edemacu and Vinay M. Shashidhar and Micheal Tuape and Dan Abudu and Beakcheol Jang and Jong Wook Kim

authors: Yongchao Long and Xian Wu and Yingying Zhang and Xianbin Wen and Yuxi Zhou and Shenda Hong

title: Confidence-Based Response Abstinence: Improving LLM Trustworthiness via Activation-Based Uncertainty Estimation
authors: Zhiqi Huang and Vivek Datla and Chenyang Zhu and Alfy Samuel and Daben Liu and Anoop Kumar and Ritesh Soni
actual_contribution: Introduces an LSTM-based confidence model over LLM FFN activations for RAG to estimate response correctness and abstain when confidence is low, with Huber-loss calibration regularization, evaluated in a financial customer-support setting.

title: Bridging External and Parametric Knowledge: Mitigating Hallucination of LLMs with Shared-Private Semantic Synergy in Dual-Stream Knowledge
authors: Yi Sui and Chaozhuo Li and Chen Zhang and Dawei song and Qiuchi Li

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Knowledge Conflict for Large Multimodal Models

actual_contribution: Introduces MMKC-Bench, a multimodal knowledge conflict benchmark for LMMs covering entity recognition, entity knowledge, and visual semantic conflicts in context-memory and inter-context settings, with analysis showing LMMs over-rely on parametric knowledge.

title: AttnTrace: Contextual Attribution of Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
authors: Yanting Wang and Runpeng Geng and Ying Chen and Jinyuan Jia
actual_contribution: AttnTrace uses LLM attention weights (with top-K token averaging and context subsampling) to trace back malicious texts in long contexts that caused prompt-injection or knowledge-corruption attack outputs, outperforming prior traceback methods.

title: Accommodate Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-augmented LLMs: Towards Robust Response Generation in the Wild
authors: Jiatai Wang and Zhiwei Xu and Di Jin and Xuewen Yang and Tao Li
actual_contribution: Analyzes knowledge conflicts in RAG from an information-theoretic perspective and proposes Swin-VIB, a sliding-window variational information bottleneck method to adapt retrieved context and reduce LLM generation uncertainty under conflicts.

title: Supportiveness-based Knowledge Rewriting for Retrieval-augmented Language Modeling
authors: Zile Qiao and Wei Ye and Yong Jiang and Tong Mo and Pengjun Xie and Weiping Li and Fei Huang and Shikun Zhang
actual_contribution: Introduces SKR, a supportiveness-based knowledge rewriter that filters noisy/misleading retrieved content and compresses context, trained via DPO to optimize downstream LLM performance.

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
authors: Sizhe Chen and Arman Zharmagambetov and Saeed Mahloujifar and Kamalika Chaudhuri and David Wagner and Chuan Guo

authors: Yuhao Wang and Ruiyang Ren and Junyi Li and Wayne Xin Zhao and Jing Liu and Ji-Rong Wen

title: Prompt Perturbation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Language Models
authors: Zhibo Hu and Chen Wang and Yanfeng Shu and Helen and Paik and Liming Zhu

actual_contribution: Proposes a gradient-based prompt perturbation attack (GGPP) that adds short prefixes to user queries to steer RAG retrievers toward targeted wrong passages and trigger factual errors, plus probe-based detection defenses.

title: Parenting: Optimizing Knowledge Selection of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Parameter Decoupling and Tailored Tuning
authors: Yongxin Xu and Ruizhe Zhang and Xinke Jiang and Yujie Feng and Yuzhen Xiao and Xinyu Ma and Runchuan Zhu and Xu Chu and Junfeng Zhao and Yasha Wang

authors: Ruizhe Zhang and Yongxin Xu and Yuzhen Xiao and Runchuan Zhu and Xinke Jiang and Xu Chu and Junfeng Zhao and Yasha Wang

title: Investigating Context-Faithfulness in Large Language Models: The Roles of Memory Strength and Evidence Style
authors: Yuepei Li and Kang Zhou and Qiao Qiao and Bach Nguyen and Qing Wang and Qi Li

title: Get my drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi and Aideen Fay and Giovanni Cherubin and Ahmed Salem and Mario Fritz and Andrew Paverd

title: Entropy-Based Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Zexuan Qiu and Zijing Ou and Bin Wu and Jingjing Li and Aiwei Liu and Irwin King

authors: Seong-Il Park and Seung-Woo Choi and Na-Hyun Kim and Jay-Yoon Lee

authors: Shu Yang and Jiayuan Su and Han Jiang and Mengdi Li and Keyuan Cheng and Muhammad Asif Ali and Lijie Hu and Di Wang

authors: Yulin Chen and Haoran Li and Zihao Zheng and Yangqiu Song and Dekai Wu and Bryan Hooi

authors: Sara Vera Marjanović and Haeun Yu and Pepa Atanasova and Maria Maistro and Christina Lioma and Isabelle Augenstein

authors: Hexiang Tan and Fei Sun and Wanli Yang and Yuanzhuo Wang and Qi Cao and Xueqi Cheng
actual_contribution: Constructs context-conflicting datasets to study how LLMs merge generated vs. retrieved contexts, finding a bias toward generated contexts driven by similarity and semantic completeness.

authors: Rustam Abdumalikov and Pasquale Minervini and Yova Kementchedjhieva

title: Adaptive Contrastive Decoding in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Handling Noisy Contexts
authors: Youna Kim and Hyuhng Joon Kim and Cheonbok Park and Choonghyun Park and Hyunsoo Cho and Junyeob Kim and Kang Min Yoo and Sang-goo Lee and Taeuk Kim

authors: Fangyuan Xu and Weijia Shi and Eunsol Choi
actual_contribution: RECOMP introduces extractive and abstractive compressors that summarize retrieved documents (or return empty strings for selective augmentation) prior to prepending to a frozen LM, reducing tokens and mitigating irrelevant-context degradation.

authors: Yunxiang Zhang and Muhammad Khalifa and Lajanugen Logeswaran and Moontae Lee and Honglak Lee and Lu Wang

authors: Dehai Min and Kailin Zhang and Tongtong Wu and Lu Cheng

authors: Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models Zhuo Chen

authors: Mehrdad Farahani; Franziska Penzkofer; Richard Johansson
actual_contribution: Mechanistic study of how LLMs arbitrate between parametric knowledge and (false) retrieved context, with a steering intervention to shift copy-vs-recall behavior. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and context compliance in RAG settings.
limitation_or_note: Focus is mechanistic/interventional rather than proposing a deployable RAG robustness method.

title: The Cost of Context: Mitigating Textual Bias in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hoin Jung; Xiaoqian Wang
actual_contribution: Identifies 'recorruption' in multimodal RAG where even oracle context degrades correct predictions due to attention collapse and positional bias, and proposes an inference-time mitigation (BAIR). Directly relevant to distraction and context-vs-internal-knowledge conflict in RAG.
limitation_or_note: Focused on multimodal (MLLM) setting rather than pure text RAG.

title: The Confidence Dichotomy: Analyzing and Mitigating Miscalibration in Tool-Use Agents
authors: Weihao Xuan; Qingcheng Zeng; Heli Qi; Yunze Xiao; Junjue Wang; Naoto Yokoya
actual_contribution: Studies how noisy evidence retrieval (web search) induces overconfidence in tool-use agents and proposes an RL framework to jointly optimize accuracy and calibration, directly relevant to calibration under unreliable evidence.
limitation_or_note: Framed as tool-use agents rather than RAG specifically, but evidence-tool analysis maps directly to retrieval noise.

title: Tackling the Inherent Difficulty of Noise Filtering in RAG
authors: Jingyu Liu; Jiaen Lin; Yong Liu
actual_contribution: Proposes a fine-tuning method to make LLMs robust to noisy/irrelevant retrieved documents, with theoretical analysis of why noise filtering is hard. Directly addresses noisy retrieval robustness.

title: Skill-RAG: Failure-State-Aware Retrieval Augmentation via Hidden-State Probing and Skill Routing
authors: Kai Wei; Raymond Li; Xi Zhu; Zhaoqian Xue; Jiaojiao Han; Jingcheng Niu; Fan Yang
actual_contribution: Skill-RAG uses hidden-state probing to detect retrieval failure states and routes among corrective skills (rewrite, decompose, focus, exit), directly addressing adaptive retrieval control, abstention, and query-evidence misalignment under OOD conditions.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on failure-recovery routing rather than adversarial or conflict settings; does not address poisoning or knowledge conflict.

title: Retromorphic Testing with Hierarchical Verification for Hallucination Detection in RAG
authors: Boxi Yu; Yuzhong Zhang; Liting Lin; Lionel Briand; Emir Muñoz
actual_contribution: Proposes a hallucination/faithfulness detector for RAG that flags unsupported or contradicted claims against retrieved context, and introduces an enhanced RAGTruth benchmark. Relevant to evaluation of context-faithfulness and detection of conflicts between generation and retrieved evidence.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on post-hoc detection rather than mitigating noisy/adversarial retrieval directly.

title: Rethinking the Reranker: Boundary-Aware Evidence Selection for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiashuo Sun; Pengcheng Jiang; Saizhuo Wang; Jiajun Fan; Heng Wang; Siru Ouyang; Ming Zhong; Yizhu Jiao; Chengsong Huang; Xueqiang Xu; Pengrui Han; Peiran Li; Jiaxin Huang; Ge Liu; Heng Ji; Jiawei Han
actual_contribution: BAR-RAG addresses RAG brittleness under noisy retrieval by training a boundary-aware reranker/selector using generator uncertainty, directly targeting robustness and evidence filtering.

title: Rethinking the Necessity of Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation through the Lens of Adaptive Listwise Ranking
authors: Jun Feng; Jiahui Tang; Zhicheng He; Hang Lv; Hongchao Gu; Hao Wang; Xuezhi Yang; Shuai Fang
actual_contribution: Proposes an adaptive listwise reranker with passage dropout that filters noisy retrieved passages and decides when retrieval is unnecessary, directly addressing noise filtering and adaptive retrieval control in RAG.
limitation_or_note: Focus is on efficiency/adaptive ranking rather than adversarial or conflict robustness.

title: ReFilter: Improving Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Gated Filter
authors: Yixin Chen; Ying Xiong; Shangyu Wu; Xiangrui Ke; Nan Guan; Chun Jason Xue
benchmark_or_task: Noisy Retrieval: Filtering and Fusion Methods
actual_contribution: Proposes a token-level gated filter to suppress irrelevant/redundant/conflicting retrieved tokens, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction in RAG and analyzing the recall-vs-performance decoupling as k grows.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on latent-fusion architecture; does not address adversarial attacks or calibration.

title: Purifying Multimodal Retrieval: Fragment-Level Evidence Selection for RAG
authors: Xihang Wang; Zihan Wang; Chengkai Huang; Cao Liu; Ke Zeng; Quan Z. Sheng; Lina Yao
actual_contribution: Proposes fragment-level evidence selection to purify noisy multimodal retrieval, directly addressing distraction and irrelevant content within retrieved documents in MRAG.
limitation_or_note: Focused on multimodal setting and selection method rather than broader robustness taxonomy.

title: OpenDecoder: Open Large Language Model Decoding to Incorporate Document Quality in RAG
authors: Fengran Mo; Zhan Su; Yuchen Hui; Jinghan Zhang; Jia Ao Sun; Zheyuan Liu; Chao Zhang; Tetsuya Sakai; Jian-Yun Nie
actual_contribution: Proposes a decoding method that integrates explicit document relevance/QPP signals to make RAG robust to noisy retrieved contexts, directly addressing noisy retrieval and control over evidence trust.

title: Multimodal Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation through Internal Representation Learning
authors: Ruoshuang Du; Xin Sun; Qiang Liu; Bowen Song; Zhongqi Chen; Weiqiang Wang; Liang Wang
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes adaptive retrieval for multimodal RAG that uses internal representations to decide when retrieved evidence is harmful vs helpful, directly addressing noisy/misleading retrieval and when-to-retrieve calibration.
limitation_or_note: Focused on multimodal VQA with reverse image retrieval, narrower than text RAG.

title: MIPIAD: Multilingual Indirect Prompt Injection Attack Defense with Qwen -- TF-IDF Hybrid and Meta-Ensemble Learning
authors: Al Muhit Muhtadi; Mostafa Rifat Tazwar
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses
actual_contribution: Proposes a multilingual defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG/tool-using LLMs and provides a large benchmark built on BIPIA, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption axis of the survey.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on input classification rather than RAG pipeline integration; empirical scope limited to English and Bangla.

title: LeakDojo: Decoding the Leakage Threats of RAG Systems
authors: Maosen Zhang; Jianshuo Dong; Boting Lu; Wenyue Li; Xiaoping Zhang; Tianwei Zhang; Han Qiu
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
actual_contribution: LeakDojo provides a configurable framework benchmarking RAG leakage attacks and defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and evaluation of RAG robustness.
limitation_or_note: Focus is on data extraction/leakage rather than poisoning or generation correctness, a narrower slice of adversarial RAG threats.

title: LatentAudit: Real-Time White-Box Faithfulness Monitoring for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Verifiable Deployment
authors: Zhe Yu; Wenpeng Xing; Meng Han
actual_contribution: Proposes a real-time faithfulness monitor for RAG that flags unsupported answers under contradictions, retrieval misses, and partial-support noise, directly relevant to calibration/abstention and robustness to unreliable evidence.
limitation_or_note: Focus on internal-state monitoring and verifiable deployment; zk-proof aspect is tangential to the survey.

title: Know When You're Wrong: Aligning Confidence with Correctness for LLM Error Detection
authors: Xie Xiaohu; Liu Xiaohu; Yao Benjamin
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes a normalized confidence score and self-evaluation for LLM error detection, with direct application to adaptive RAG (selective retrieval when uncertain). Also analyzes calibration impacts of SFT/RL/DPO and proposes a fix.
limitation_or_note: Adaptive RAG is a demonstration rather than the primary focus; broader scope is general LLM calibration.

title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance
authors: Eunbyeol Cho; Yunseung Lee; Mirae Kim; Jeewon Yang; Youngjun Kwak; Edward Choi
actual_contribution: Introduces a multi-turn RAG hallucination detection benchmark with a taxonomy covering contradictions, unverifiable claims, irrelevance, and justified abstention—directly relevant to evaluating RAG robustness, context faithfulness, and refusal calibration.
limitation_or_note: Domain-specific (Korean finance), which may limit generality.

title: ICON: Indirect Prompt Injection Defense for Agents based on Inference-Time Correction
authors: Che Wang; Fuyao Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Ziqi Zhang; Yinghui Wang; Longtao Huang; Jianbo Gao; Zhong Chen; Wei Yang Bryan Lim
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses
actual_contribution: Proposes an inference-time defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in tool-augmented LLM agents, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved content in RAG-style settings.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on agent tool-use rather than classical RAG QA; relevance to retrieval robustness is via IPI in retrieved content.

title: How You Ask Matters! Adaptive RAG Robustness to Query Variations
authors: Yunah Jang; Megha Sundriyal; Kyomin Jung; Meeyoung Cha
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Introduces a benchmark evaluating Adaptive RAG robustness to semantically equivalent query variations, measuring stability of retrieval decisions (when to retrieve) and answer quality—directly relevant to calibration/control and evaluation under unreliable inputs.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on query-side variation rather than evidence-side noise/conflict/attacks.

title: How Retrieved Context Shapes Internal Representations in RAG
authors: Samuel Yeh; Sharon Li
actual_contribution: Analyzes how relevant, distracting, and random retrieved documents shape LLM internal representations and downstream behavior in RAG, connecting noise/distraction to abstention and parametric-vs-retrieved interactions.
limitation_or_note: Representation-level analysis rather than a new robustness method or benchmark.

title: Hidden in Memory: Sleeper Memory Poisoning in LLM Agents
authors: Sidharth Pulipaka; Stanislau Hlebik; Leonidas Raghav; Sahar Abdelnabi; Vyas Raina; Ivaxi Sheth; Mario Fritz
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection
actual_contribution: Studies indirect prompt injection that poisons persistent memory of LLM agents, causing delayed retrieval-driven malicious behavior. Relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval/memory stores in RAG-like pipelines.
limitation_or_note: Focus is on agent memory rather than classic RAG corpora; relevance is via analogy to retrieval poisoning and indirect injection.

title: Fact-Checking with Large Language Models via Probabilistic Certainty and Consistency
authors: Haoran Wang; Maryam Khalid; Qiong Wu; Jian Gao; Cheng Cao
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
actual_contribution: Proposes a confidence-based adaptive routing mechanism deciding when to rely on parametric knowledge vs trigger retrieval/deep search, directly addressing calibration and control of retrieval under uncertainty.
limitation_or_note: Focused on fact-checking rather than general RAG QA; robustness to noisy/adversarial evidence not the central concern.

title: Facet-Level Tracing of Evidence Uncertainty and Hallucination in RAG
authors: Passant Elchafei; Monorama Swain; Shahed Masoudian; Markus Schedl
benchmark_or_task: Evaluation and Diagnostics of Evidence Usage
actual_contribution: Introduces a facet-level diagnostic framework that traces evidence uncertainty and retrieval-generation misalignment in RAG, characterizing failure modes such as evidence absence, misalignment, and parametric-knowledge overrides. Directly relevant to knowledge conflict, uncertainty, and evaluation of RAG faithfulness.
limitation_or_note: Diagnostic/analysis rather than a defense or new method; limited datasets.

title: EnterpriseRAG-Bench: A RAG Benchmark for Company Internal Knowledge
authors: Yuhong Sun; Joachim Rahmfeld; Chris Weaver; Weijia Chen; Roshan Desai; Wenxi Huang; Mark H. Butler
actual_contribution: Introduces an enterprise RAG benchmark explicitly featuring noisy/misfiled documents, near-duplicates, conflicting information, and 'info not found' questions testing abstention—directly aligned with robustness, conflict resolution, and unknown-claim evaluation.
limitation_or_note: Synthetic enterprise focus; not a method or defense paper.

title: DeepEra: A Deep Evidence Reranking Agent for Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated Question Answering
authors: Haotian Chen; Qingqing Long; Siyu Pu; Xiao Luo; Wei Ju; Meng Xiao; Yuanchun Zhou; Jianghua Zhao; Xuezhi Wang
actual_contribution: Proposes a reranking agent and benchmark (SciRAG-SSLI) specifically targeting semantically similar but logically irrelevant distractor passages in RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction robustness.
limitation_or_note: Focused on scientific QA domain; reranking-centric rather than full robustness taxonomy.

title: D$^2$Plan: Dual-Agent Dynamic Global Planning for Complex Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
authors: Kangcheng Luo; Tinglang Wu; Yansong Feng
actual_contribution: Proposes a dual-agent planning method to mitigate distraction by irrelevant retrieved evidence and ineffective query construction in multi-hop RAG, with a Purifier explicitly filtering noisy retrievals and adaptive re-retrieval.
limitation_or_note: Focus is on multi-hop QA performance rather than systematic robustness analysis or calibration.

title: ConflictRAG: Detecting and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Chenyu Wang; Yingmin Liu; Yang Shu
actual_contribution: Proposes a conflict-aware RAG pipeline that detects, classifies, and resolves inter-document and parametric-contextual conflicts, plus a CARS evaluation metric—directly relevant to the knowledge conflict and evaluation themes.
limitation_or_note: Suspicious arXiv ID (2605) suggests possible metadata issue; self-constructed benchmark has acknowledged bias.

title: CAR: Query-Guided Confidence-Aware Reranking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhipeng Song; Yizhi Zhou; Xiangyu Kong; Jiulong Jiao; Xuezhou Ye; Chunqi Gao; Xueqing Shi; Yuhang Zhou; Heng Qi
benchmark_or_task: Calibration and Control / Filtering Noisy Retrieval
actual_contribution: CAR uses generator confidence (semantic consistency of sampled answers) to rerank documents, filtering noisy/unhelpful evidence and gating intervention based on query-level uncertainty—directly addressing calibration-aware control over retrieval and mitigating noisy retrieval in RAG.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on reranking; doesn't address adversarial or conflict cases.

title: AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification
authors: Tian Zhang; Yiwei Xu; Juan Wang; Keyan Guo; Xiaoyang Xu; Bowen Xiao; Quanlong Guan; Jinlin Fan; Jiawei Liu; Zhiquan Liu; Hongxin Hu
benchmark_or_task: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses
actual_contribution: Proposes an inference-time defense against indirect prompt injection in tool/retrieval-augmented LLM agents, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved content.
limitation_or_note: Focuses on agent workflows rather than pure RAG QA; IPI defense via causal diagnostics is agent-centric.

title: Adaptive Guidance for Retrieval-Augmented Masked Diffusion Models
authors: Jaemin Kim; Jong Chul Ye
actual_contribution: Proposes adaptive guidance for masked diffusion RAG that dynamically calibrates trust between retrieved context and parametric prior via SNR, directly addressing knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval.
limitation_or_note: Focused on diffusion language models, a niche substrate compared to autoregressive RAG.

title: A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: Targeted Routing Hijacking in Federated RAG
authors: Junjie Mu; Qiongxiu Li
actual_contribution: Introduces a novel routing-stage attack on Federated RAG where malicious clients forge semantic profiles, causing missing evidence, poisoning, and hallucinations, and proposes a trust-aware defense. Fits adversarial corruption and retrieval robustness themes.
limitation_or_note: Focused on federated RAG setting, which is narrower than mainstream RAG robustness.

title: "I Don't Know" -- Towards Appropriate Trust with Certainty-Aware Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Daan Di Scala; Maaike de Boer; Pınar Yolum
actual_contribution: Proposes CERTA, a certainty-aware RAG that self-reflects on uncertainty across question-context-answer relevance to enable abstention/hedging, and introduces a benchmark with relevant/incomplete/irrelevant contexts. Directly relevant to calibration, abstention, and noisy retrieval evaluation.
limitation_or_note: Small benchmark (90 pairs) focused on non-objective questions; framing emphasizes trust/values more than retrieval robustness per se.
